and layout dependencies remain responsible for their intermediate identities.

queries. Preparation clones checked Foundation entities into compiler-owned
execution snapshots, preserving source signatures and later mutation analysis.

their source identities. Calls resume at the interpreter task boundary after
arguments have evaluated, without repeating their effects. Focused fixtures

### Remaining work after the type-value checkpoint (requested clean stopping point)

The user requested stopping after a clean committed/pushed checkpoint, with the
remaining work recorded here. Do not start vectors or claim the source-defined
type architecture is complete. The next session should continue in this order:

1. **Consolidate the prelude in types.tower.** Foundation already imports that
   file, but it currently forwards to thirteen scalar modules plus types/integer.
   Move those definitions and shared integer constructors into the one file and
   remove the forwarding imports/directory. Audit compiler_project_files.tower,
   bootstrap resource collection, browser build.mjs, builtin/recipe filters and
   build-packaging tests before deleting paths. type_binding_checks currently
   overrides types/i32.tower; change it to override the actual consolidated
   prelude while preserving the other named types. Preserve the test proving a
   changed i32 source definition controls layout and representation. Regenerate
   complete resources/pins and compiler-project assets through the documented
   build path; a file move must not strand users on stale packaged imports.

2. **Inventory and specify the type/operation protocol.** Audit semantic_types,
   semantic_values, semantic_definitions, semantic_expressions, type_primitives,
   semantic_layout, format_foundation, the interpreters and backend/lowering.
   Separate named-language policy from the irreducible Foundation operation
   contract. Remaining scalar tags describe private execution representations;
   deleting all machine-operation knowledge is not the objective. Hardcoded
   behavior attached to the names i32/f32/etc must disappear. Record the owner
   of identity, representation, target layout/ABI, literal defaults/construction,
   conversions, operators and reflection, with one canonical Foundation spelling
   per semantic operation. Attributes are typed metadata identified by their
   bound nominal type; spellings or arbitrary annotations do not grant behavior.

3. **Execute representation constructors with ordinary inputs.** Type functions
   can currently select/return existing types, but integer_type(local_width, 1)
   and other general executed constructors remain unsupported. Route creation
   through the ordinary interpreter and shared dependency graph, suspending for
   coordinator-owned interning/publication. Keep query state and scratch on ECS
   components, target/profile/revision identity explicit and worker reads frozen.
   No separate constant folder or process-global type registry. Specify which
   construction capabilities are compile-stage-only and diagnose runtime misuse;
   an ordinary runtime type value cannot change existing static storage layout.

4. **Unify constructor/staging compatibility paths.** Module var Name:type is
   still a transparent static alias; local var value:type is ordinary storage.
   T:type parameters still request specialization, while type_type() parameters
   carry ordinary values. Restricted straight-return/nominal constructors retain
   early identity publication and a separate shape-based registration path.
   Design and migrate these together without losing recursive nominal identity,
   forward headers, generic inference or deterministic source diagnostics. Do not
   solve the distinction using parser-side symbol lookup or a second type graph.

5. **Move every named primitive's full policy into types.tower.** Define shared
   integer/floating implementations and associate ordinary typed Tower functions
   for operators, conversions and literals. Each named width instantiates/selects
   those implementations rather than implicitly receiving all operators merely
   from integer_type. Foundation operations supply explicit fixed-width wrapping,
   checked conversion and strict floating semantics; operator functions can call
   these named operations without recursively resolving their own operator.
   Resolve operators through the shared protocol into typed calls/operations.
   Optimizations may recognize proven primitive implementations and inline/lower
   them, but must not silently replace user-defined behavior. Literal defaults
   are still signed-32/binary64 compiler policy today and need an explicit source
   policy. Preserve exact typing, sequencing, lazy compounds, signed minima,
   negative zero, rounding, subnormals and NaN rules across staging and targets.

6. **Migrate the other existing type families.** Apply the same construction,
   operation, layout and reflection contracts to bool/void/usize, pointers,
   references, arrays, nominal structs/enums, function values and type values.
   Keep raw Foundation storage/alias/lifetime semantics separate from future
   Stronghold initialization and ownership restrictions. Pointer/reference work
   must not invent safety or ownership guarantees. Use the same checked nodes
   and protocol calls for surface syntax and explicit constructor functions.

7. **Close representation and backend boundaries.** Current metatype indexes
   are private four-byte execution/module storage. Direct metatype foreign and
   export signatures are rejected, but recursive aggregate/callback/opaque-memory
   transport needs a complete explicit legality policy. Do not expose indexes as
   stable cross-module identities. LLVM scalar reconstruction currently falls
   back to canonical profile 0 for programs containing type values; direct import
   rejects their reconstruction. C/BrightScript do not implement type values.
   Either preserve full descriptors through an applicable transformation or retain
   the canonical graph; never turn type identities into public integer constants.
   Keep .towerbc reconstruction/cache checks and captured type/function relocation.

8. **Validate each coherent migration before adopting it in compiler sources.**
   Extend Tower fixtures for protocol selection, exact bits/traps, nominal/alias
   identity, pointer and aggregate layout, executed and untaken dependencies,
   mutation/escape proofs, generic recursion, cycles and recursive ABI rejection.
   Check canonical fixed points, both interpreters, native/Wasm and serial/real
   overlapping worker execution. Keep source diagnostics stable across worker
   counts and drain views/stages on cancellation/failure. Profile whole-program
   source-binding scans before claiming they are cheap; refine dependency demand

  can change results. Apply these principles to Tower without importing native
  implementations or borrowing the sources' performance numbers.

### B2 finite unit snapshots and joined-boundary failures (2026-11-22)

Implementation draft, not publication evidence: frontend_units_create_bounded
accepts a positive finite declared-byte cap. Its exact immutable resource/source
copies reserve the complete new capacity (including terminators) before allocating,
while the old receipt remains live. Only a complete replacement commits; allocation,
capacity or length-overflow failure leaves the old buffers/configuration intact.
The original create API retains an explicitly named compatibility policy. Backend
streaming shares the frontend ledger; a later standalone backend may select its
own cap for target/object retention. Opaque LLVM allocation precedes availability
of its output length: the coordinator reserves exposed output before publication
or closes the rejected LLVM owner. This does not bound parser/LLVM heaps or RSS.

The actual driver selects the finite API with --unit-retained-bytes. The named
256MiB default is provisional pending representative known-retention measurements;
positive decimal overrides require --unit. Original driver input copies, import
caches and linker allocations are outside this service's known-byte count.

### 2026-11-22: A2 shared budget ledger and concurrent instrumentation

The agreed WorkBudget/WorkReservation core is now implemented in
library/work_budget.tower. This is admission accounting, not a second scheduler
or an enforced process-memory limit. Positive lane grants count executing callers;
nested extra grants allow minimum zero. A grant with zero lanes and zero bytes
succeeds with an inactive default receipt and needs no release. A bytes-only
grant remains active until the known retained allocation is reclaimed. Every
active receipt matches owner/revision/slot/generation and recorded sizes before
release, so copied receipts cannot release a newer occupant's slot. Disposal
refuses live grants and retains the last revision against reuse.

One coordinator needs no gate. Multiple coordinators bind an immutable gate and
typed enter/leave callbacks before dispatch, using existing host semaphores.
Only short ledger transactions hold the gate; no capacity wait, execution or
join occurs while holding it. Concurrent callers receive their own error result
and obtain counters through a locked snapshot, rather than reading a shared last
error. The gate outlives all worlds, grants and borrowers and closes after ledger
disposal. This contract was proposed through status before B2/A1/B1 adoption.
B2 owns world/outer integration; B1 parser waves and A1 semantic dispatch remain
coordinated pending work. Unmeasured integration is not claimed complete.

The first coordinator-only version passed deterministic 8,192-operation
reference accounting, copy/double/foreign/stale/reused-revision rejection,
busy disposal, limit/overflow and cleanup checks. Added optional/bytes-only
coverage after the common API follow-up. The four-thread fixture holds explicit
outer grants and exercises 8,192 concurrent extra-grant/release/stale-copy cycles
with real production allocation and a simultaneous-entry barrier. Its first
execution failed a test's checked usize-to-u8 conversion at round256; changed
the fixture's byte pattern to round modulo256, leaving the ledger unchanged.
The corrected native test passes. Three ASan and three TSan executions then pass
with all emitted fixture and executable-runtime definitions instrumented, exact
output0 and real allocator/pthread/semaphore transport. This is ledger/transport
evidence, not full compiler acceptance or a proof about every thread schedule.

The new opt-in tests/layout_frontier_profile.tower invokes actual sem_layout_execute
on canonical world-owned type entities and ordered, uniquely owned fields. It

ledger dispose. This is a targeted layout microbenchmark, not end-to-end compiler
performance or a second scheduler. Shared ledger includes the caller and each
world limit is1/2/4/8. Stable payloads remain sparse; no new noalias assertion.

New own tests/entity_stage_concurrent.tower closes a focused coverage gap left
by the serial entity_stage_ownership/fault fixtures. It reuses EntityStage,
WorkGraph, WorkPool and WorkBudget, no scheduler/allocator substitute. Each of
160 trials reserves caller+workers, takes access claims/tickets and leases before
dispatch. Private stage pages allocate on2/4 real pthreads behind an entry
barrier. The input target loses its last ordinary reference while pinned; each
worker queues payload holds without touching shared reference counts. After all
joins the coordinator holds every stage twice (idempotence), closes the last
input view, publishes/discards, settles tickets, then releases lane receipts.
Cases include successful publication, cancellation while admitted, worker failure,
duplicate named-member publication rejection, and cancellation after partial
admission. Cancelled tickets cannot publish success. Every finalizer resolves
explicit store context and runs on its owning coordinator thread; no mutable
ambient test counter. Ordered children/payloads and exact empty-store teardown
are checked, including releasing private pools before stage destruction.

### L1 captured aggregate consumer: current reproduction and joint implementation

Current-v3 public-pin compiler d09bad2c15560ccf00b70f4b7ae8987f1ffc377e745f17e79afac4fa6dc4fe44 independently matches L2's binary. Exact global Pair capture and local Pair capture fail at 1:125 and 1:138, respectively, at both one and four workers; the independent expected outputs remain 7,8 and15. The original address-derived known-binding negative instead succeeds and prints32. These are reproduced failures, not accepted behavior. Raw sources/results are L1/aggregate_capture_exact_v3.tower, local_aggregate_capture_exact_v3.tower and logs/own_v3_*. The complete d09 compiler, execution/LR runners and adjacent resources were preserved under /root/.cache/tower/l1_before_aggregate_inputs_20261122 before changing the consumer.

The producer already publishes flattened, typed, canonical scalar projections of a completed aggregate. The consumer previously rejected every captured-input address; scalar substitution could not supply the aggregate storage needed by ordinary lowering. The joint change reuses that existing projection vector as IMValueProjection, borrowed only by the exact required producer. It adds no initializer evaluator, semantic IR or constant folder. On first reached use, the ordinary interpreter copies published leaves into its own target-byte stack allocation, rematerializing type/function references through its own indexes. Empty aggregates have an explicit aggregate flag; null pointer leaves remain legal and non-null raw pointer leaves remain rejected. Private padding is initialized but gains no public semantic value.

Copies belong to the consuming frame. Caller copies survive nested returns and statement-cache resets; ended-frame copies are forgotten before stack reuse. A retained aggregate root keeps its bytes/initialization state through existing result publication. All strict scalar writes and ordinary copy/fill instructions pass the same immutable-range check. Storage metadata publishes only after every field has copied successfully; failure remains an invocation failure followed by normal disposal. A1's publisher997aa4c9 retains borrowed projection arrays until every consumer invocation has been disposed. Optional known_producer metadata cannot borrow required capture proof/storage.

A1's separate capture policy595209af derives the exact capture producer role before dispatch and freezes its relocation flag in work metadata. It preserves inferred-versus-required input roles and direct explicit-stage address policy. The interpreter therefore rejects executed address-derived capture values without syntactically rejecting an untaken branch. The reviewed42-case lifecycle fixture preserves the original30 cases and adds12 policy cases; A1's12-case pass is owner evidence, not a full42-case or L1 runtime pass.

### 2026-11-22 A2 retained-buffer design and first implementation draft

The coordinator identified two required remaining capabilities after the coherent
native milestone: physical retained-buffer accounting and a selectable packed
component payload policy. These are required work, not optional optimizations.
B1's complete parser allocation inventory was read. FIRST/propagation buffers
swap into retained results, LR rows/gotos move into runtime tables, and closure
hash growth is data dependent even in serial execution. Charging only a parser
worker-count estimate cannot cover these owners.

The first implementation draft is `library/work_buffer.tower` plus
`library/work_vector.tower`. It uses the existing synchronized WorkBudget and
compiler_buffer allocator, with a separate byte-only receipt attached to each
physical allocation. It reserves the full replacement before allocation, copies
only initialized bytes, frees old storage before releasing the old grant, and
preserves the old owner on overflow, denied admission or allocation failure.
Move/swap transfers the whole allocation receipt without charging it again.
Outer frozen snapshots retain B2's existing grant; nested borrowed bytes are not
charged again. Nested newly allocated scratch/results receive their own grant.
Lane release at join/publication does not free retained bytes.

The generic vector has a distinct type so ordinary vector free/realloc cannot
silently discard its compiler allocation header or grant. It preserves the
existing min-eight/doubling growth and explicit element ownership. A result API
returns Capacity versus Invalid versus Memory; the bool convenience is retained.
Alignment is an explicit host allocator contract, not inferred from a view or

Implemented the previously proposed shared WorkBudgetError result APIs in
work_pool and compiler_kernel, preserving bool wrappers. The useful distinction
is ownership: Busy entry does not drain preexisting jobs; valid drained entry
owns and joins every admitted batch worker before returning. Semaphore creation
failure is Memory before any execution. Defensive admission failure returns Busy
with joined peers, but may have executed every queued job: never replay or
publish partial outputs. Empty input leaves ownership/receipt untouched. Invalid
entry likewise leaves the old receipt. A valid call resets the private/coordinator
receipt, and close preserves it after freeing storage. Generic projection rejects
null array/first job before taking the embedded kernel address. No scheduler,
queue allocation, shared graph mutation or noalias claim was introduced.

Implemented the previously proposed shared WorkBudgetError result APIs in
work_pool and compiler_kernel, preserving bool wrappers. The useful distinction
is ownership: Busy entry does not drain preexisting jobs; valid drained entry
owns and joins every admitted batch worker before returning. Semaphore creation
failure is Memory before any execution. Defensive admission failure returns Busy
with joined peers, but may have executed every queued job: never replay or
publish partial outputs. Empty input leaves ownership/receipt untouched. Invalid
entry likewise leaves the old receipt. A valid call resets the private/coordinator
receipt, and close preserves it after freeing storage. Generic projection rejects
null array/first job before taking the embedded kernel address. No scheduler,
queue allocation, shared graph mutation or noalias claim was introduced.

deferred structural commands from direct component writes, and derives required

stable SemanticEntry/work payloads and dense pointer/query indexes satisfy
different requirements; neither a dense handle array nor the new WorkGraph
borrowed view proves packed Foundation payloads or reduced fragmentation.

Cleanup needs phase-specific ownership, not a blanket stage discard. Body,
declaration, executable, evaluation preparation and lowering may have installed
links from leased canonical payloads to private-stage nodes. Join all peers and
publish those structural ownership stages before releasing leases; suppress
successful semantic readiness and external result publication on transport
failure. Body workers also transfer allocations/lists, pending evaluations,
aliases and lexical continuations; these owners must be adopted or disposed
without resuming statements. Iteration resolution transfers scratch before
ordinary signature preparation; failed transport must skip that preparation and
retire its arrays. Flow and known analysis own private result vectors and no
structural stage. Interpreter invocations must all retire before borrowed
producer projections. Current cancellation remains at joined frontiers, without
unsynchronized WorkGraph mutation or an invented bounded whole-kernel latency.

### A1 joined dependency-request failure callers (2026-11-23)

Implementation under review: b58489fe plus the unchanged, ROOT-routed L2

A joined type request may return zero after the graph has failed. The old
caller asserted while finishing that invalid ticket. A failed generic-body
request likewise flowed into body discovery and executable registration; the
consumer could then suspend on zero. The declaration pump's empty batch only
checked failure when generic execution returned progress, allowing false idle
success. The fix stops registration on the sticky program/graph receipt, checks
failure independently of progress, and retires only valid evaluation tickets.
After all workers join, it disposes every remaining invocation and withholds
peer/alias publication after the first global failure. Existing source-ordered
ordinary evaluation failure selection remains separate.

The new semantic_query_failure_checks.tower uses real world ownership, the
ordinary interpreter, generic registry/header APIs and a budget-bound WorkGraph.

constructor/function suspension before coordinator cleanup; a peer must really
complete. It exhausts remaining ledger bytes from the actual snapshot and task
capacity, never a guessed allocation count. Twelve cases cover pointer widths
4/8 and workers1/4 across constructor, body and empty declaration failure.
They assert Capacity, drained graph/pool, disposed invocations, no peer value
publication, repeated failure without entity/component growth, and zero final
ledger grants/world ownership. This is targeted failure evidence, not general
scheduler scaling or production graph-budget adoption.

### A2 stable free-slot reuse implementation and focused closure (2026-11-23 09:24Z)

Implemented the reviewed proposal in entities/entity_types/entity_stage only.
EntityComponentPage adds a one-based free head. After all published index removal
and lifecycle callbacks, a dead descriptor's type_index stores the next free slot.
Allocation consumes that chain before increasing the high-water used count; a
page detaches only when live reaches capacity. A first free on a detached page
links it to its owner's current private pool or published store pool. Joined stage
publication transfers partial page links after clearing all staged owner pointers,
before freeing the stage. Discard retains private detach/last-live cleanup. No
surviving component or payload moves. Removed borrowed pointers expire as before;
reuse does not supply safe stale-pointer handles or inferred noalias.

retain the old realloc allocation, and free(null) to do nothing. Therefore a

and ix_deallocate removes ownership before inserting the coalesced free range.

free bookkeeping would let later valid free/coalescing avoid a new allocation
under exhausted allowance. Realloc must admit this tracking before moving bytes
or retiring its old block. No dual-reservation transaction or new allocator
framework is implemented or claimed; required metadata retention and measured
cost must be evaluated. Cached strings and value/address/sequencing maps need
separate exact-offset failure and no-replay handling at their actual callers.

refreshes that pointer only after its producer publishes, rather than consuming
the pre-registration body. Stages publish after every admitted peer joins and
before ticket completion. Partial take discards undispatched stages; checked
transport/observe/finish failures cancel receipts after joining. Ordinary errors
remain on the function's work component across waits. Selection retains the old
priority (signature phase before expression phase, source order within each).
The lifecycle pump exposes Progress/Waiting/Complete/Failed. Only its owning,
quiescent wrapper diagnoses unfinished producers/cycles. Existing single-phase
pump entry points retain their progress convention and are still supported.

### A2 queued-stage ownership prerequisite, 2026-11-23 (blocked, not implemented)

Reviewed integrated `afca69b171c790ce9386ae85c3f3d493d21cec59` after the requested
`git pull --rebase=merges --autostash --ff-only`. No owned build was running;
the worktree was clean. This bounded task did not resume the former goal or
inventory campaign. The explicit task leaves final deployment with ROOT.

Source inspection confirms `entity_stage_hold` increments every unheld queue
entry without checking exhaustion. The queue stores target entities and a held
prefix, not the payload locations whose finalizers release them. Publish and
discard both invoke that unchecked hold. Duplicate targets require cumulative
accounting; checking each against its initial count is insufficient. Existing
queue-slice alias rebasing already handles queue growth and must be preserved.

The only production queue writer found by `rg` is
`compiler/syntax_provenance.tower:syntax_origin_copy_staged_result`. It builds a
temporary entity array, queues it, installs borrowed expansion/splice pointers in
`SyntaxOrigin`, then disposes the temporary array. Its ordinary finalizer releases
all those pointers. The lifecycle dispatcher supplies no cancellation operation.
Consequently a failed checked hold cannot safely proceed into today's discard:
unheld payload pointers would still be released. Skipping finalizers would leak
their owned buffers. Suppressing selected entity releases is also insufficient:
`syntax_trace_release` may detach and traverse a uniquely owned history before
calling `entity_release`. A pin protects lifetime, not ownership of that history.

**Prerequisite:** include this immediate provenance producer in the ownership
batch, or have ROOT supply its cancellation contract. The current grant permits
library stage/helpers/fixtures and the immediate generic-body hold caller; it
does not permit changing `syntax_provenance.tower`. No production edits were
made across that boundary, and no unsafe preflight-only patch was installed.

Proposed protocol (design only): each queued payload registers stable private
cancellation metadata before installing borrowed references. A checked hold
acquires all pending references, counting repeated targets, or returns the exact
error with that pending ownership untransferred. Already-held ownership remains
distinct. After joins, discard cancels only unheld borrowed fields before ordinary
finalization; held fields release normally. Source owners/views remain live
through either outcome. Queue admission and metadata allocation must be atomic,
and retries must not retain twice. Existing compatibility wrappers and empty
queue paths must remain available. The precise API is not implemented or agreed.

Caller handoff: production search found publish callers in `semantic_body_work`,
`semantic_declarations`, `semantic_evaluation_work`, `semantic_lowering_work`,
`semantic_execution_work` and `semantic_generic_body_work`; declarations also
exist in `semantic_context`. The generic-body pump joins, holds every stage, then
closes its view; its deferred discard must safely handle hold failure before
that view closes. The execution pump currently closes its view before publishing;
ROOT owns its checked-hold adoption. The remaining publish callers need their
actual queued-reference behavior checked when the protocol is integrated; this
call-site inventory is not a completed substantive review of those pipelines.
Twenty test/profile files reference hold/publish/discard/queue APIs, including
the existing stage ownership, result, concurrent, reentrant, page reuse and
generic clone fixtures. No fixtures or generic harness files changed.

The previous driver drained every lowering query before requesting late stage
execution. `semantic_phase_work.tower` now records two root-owned WorkGraph
joins without another function registry/context layout: signature publication
waits for AggregatePrepare/KnownSnapshot; full canonical lowering also waits for
every registered Lowering producer. Explicit EvaluationPrepare depends on the
signature join and its lexical owner's lowering. Already prepared/suspended
Evaluation tickets observe or suspend on those same prerequisites. Inferred
execution retains the full lowering join because it can call canonical function
bodies directly. Explicit calls retain ROOT's lazy executable snapshot requests;
only reached reads/calls demand producers. No eager branch dependency scan.

The lifecycle services one existing mixed lowering frontier, joins and publishes,
then services ready evaluation and its existing dependency pumps before returning
to more lowering. This removes the blanket lowering-before-explicit-evaluation
barrier: the new fixture completes a stage while the last ordinary lowering task
is still Ready, with function count derived from SemanticPreparationWindow. It
also completes independent and nested dependent stages while unrelated lowering
waits, retains an explicit stage behind its own owner, and holds inferred stages
behind the canonical join. Evaluation diagnostics stay private until lowering's
phase/source priority settles. Repeated waits preserve invocation steps, memory,
frames and component count; terminal calls retain no running tickets/workers.
No evaluation/lowering kernels execute simultaneously: joined windows remain
necessary for shared aliases, ABI records and canonical payload publication.
Existing worker/buffer ceilings and fast serial transport are reused.

Implemented `entity_stage_references_cancellable_result(stage, nodes, count,
cancel: function(void, void*), context)` with private stable payload cancellation
records admitted atomically before borrowed fields are installed. The existing
queue validation and self-alias rebasing remain shared by both admission APIs.
The provenance callback clears only expansion/splice pointers; the usual
finalizer still frees owned vectors. Empty/null-only admissions allocate no
cancellation metadata. No global state, alternate graph or release suppression.

`entity_stage_hold_result(stage): WorkBudgetError` acquires the entire pending
suffix without allocation. Temporary increments cumulatively account for
duplicate targets; failure restores every increment without reclaiming pinned
zero-count inputs. `held` advances only on success. Invalid stage/held bounds
return Invalid, a newly leased queued target returns Busy, and counter exhaustion
returns Exhausted. Earlier held ownership is unchanged. Publication reserves
component-type ownership before the queued transaction, detecting their combined
count when a queued target is also a component type. Failure restores temporary
type counts and unprepares table rows; no semantic publication has occurred.

`entity_stage_discard_result(stage): WorkBudgetError` cancels unheld borrowed
fields before ordinary finalizers. For a legacy queue without cancellation
metadata it first performs checked hold; failure preserves the entire stage and
returns the exact error. Legacy void hold/discard wrappers trap on failure,
instead of wrapping counts, leaking silently or finalizing unowned pointers.
Already-held/empty discard skips the cancellation scans. Producers must keep
callback contexts stable, forbid queue mutation/releasing targets in callbacks,
and retain source owners/views through hold success or failure cleanup.

The generic-body pump now drains and discards every peer before its last view
close on hold failure, then propagates the exact dispatch/hold receipt. A real
provenance fixture verifies repeated/null splices, an unchanged previous-history
chain, no published clone and complete stage/world/budget cleanup on Exhausted
at target widths4/8. Shared stage tests cover held-prefix preservation, zero-count
rollback, alias input, retry idempotence, combined type/payload counts, legacy
safe failure/retry and finalizer totals. The concurrent fixture uses the real
allocator/transport and the new admission API; its original overlap and ownership
oracles remain. The exact semantic import allowlist and its existing fixture add
only `entity_stage_hold_result`, the immediate ABI consequence of the caller edit.

## D2 suffix-FIRST reuse — frozen 2e77d747, 2026-11-23

Implemented the bounded follow-up to87a5da1a on published
`2e77d74713bb44fd74b8605919c1b1b68eefaf1f`, including B1's complete81381afb
state-core optimization and current A1/A2/L2 ownership changes. B1's
lr_states/lr_state_work and their tests are preserved. No new grammar authority,
cache format, global mutable state, state-interning order or scheduler.

`LRAnalysis` now owns one typed suffix-index pointer. A checked WorkBuffer holds
its descriptor, production-base array and dense suffix records; a second holds
flat sorted SymbolRanges. Counts, offsets, alignment and overflow checks derive
from actual productions/types. Only suffixes following nonterminals are populated.
The serial FIRST helper and parallel dependency pump publish this index only after
convergence/joins. Parser calls supply their world's WorkBudget; standalone
analysis explicitly uses null. All partial index storage retires on typed
Memory/Capacity/Invalid failure; the same analysis can retry. Published buffers
are immutable through worker borrows and retire with the analysis after joins.
Existing raw analysis/FIRST/scratch allocations are not a whole-world memory cap.

`lr_suffix_result` copies the precomputed exact ranges to its existing private
scratch and inserts incoming lookahead only when the suffix is nullable. Range
overlap remains distinct, not interval union. Production bases distinguish shared
symbol spans with different ends. Unreachable invalid references retain per-row
errors until a closure demands them; FIRST does not begin rejecting such tails.
Pre-completion standalone closure calls retain the original uncached path.

Measured the unchanged caller before editing production: new `lr-suffix` selector
in the existing frontend profile constructs32 seeds (including LRTokenPropagation

### B1 urgent scratch ownership identity lookup (2026-11-23)

Base36fe44884eec2ab9db08f92bd8f2494cf41c2982; required pull advanced only docs,
no surviving owned work. B2's b21c13c7 evidence above identified228s incomplete
semantics self-compilation versus21.7s known-good. Audited all sem_push_checked
call sites: sem_list arena vectors, c.scan, raw lexical/stack/component/program
vectors and borrowed lexical lists all use the same API. Arbitrary vector
headers cannot safely be cast to scratch descriptors. Audited sem_list,
sem_scratch_private/snapshot, body/declaration/iteration scratch transfer and
sem_scratch_append/dispose. Existing linked registration at the tail caused each
push (even c.scan and nonmembers) to walk all retained lists and lexical parents.

Implemented one intrusive digital search tree in the existing owned descriptors:
SemanticScratchList adds two child pointers; SemanticScratch adds one root.
Exact address equality establishes membership before any owned storage access.
Each search level consumes one address bit, giving a pointer-width-plus-root
bound per lexical owner, independent of live-list count or allocation order.
Registration uses only the descriptor's existing checked arena grant. No hidden
header, guessed membership, allocating hash resize, last-list cache, global
state or semantic representation. Scan uses its explicit buffer immediately;
nonmembers retain the original raw-vector path. WorkBuffer growth/typed first
cause and all caller APIs remain unchanged. sem_scratch_find exposes a readonly
lookup and optional caller-owned probe count, with no shared mutable metrics.

Snapshot resets the private index and borrows parent indexes read-only. Existing
workers mutate only their private descriptors; exclusive lexical pushes retain
the original storage owner. After workers join, append validates arena/budget
compatibility before relinking source descriptors into the receiving index. It
allocates nothing, preserves vector addresses/buffers and empties source ownership;
whole-owner transfer copies its root. Self-append is a no-op. Disposal still uses
the independent ownership chain, frees WorkBuffers, then arena, then clears the
index. Added metadata is charged by actual descriptor/component sizes, with no
new allocator or budget bypass. L2 sem_node/sem_create admission region untouched.

already immutable LR(0) items, borrowing D2's completed suffix-FIRST index.
Each kernel starts a private reachability queue; nullable suffixes propagate
lookahead and nonempty FIRST contributes spontaneous seeds. Empty nonnullable
FIRST does not activate otherwise unreachable dot-zero items. Each active item
is visited once per state; source order, nullable reductions, recursive start
kernels, propagation sentinel and the existing fixed-point/action algorithm are
preserved. No second grammar, cross-version identity or persistent cache exists.
The maximum-state-sized queue/flags use one checked WorkBuffer charged to the
explicit world budget, retire before dispatch, and unwind the unpublished graph
on the first exact error. Existing standalone APIs and cached closure wrappers
remain available. Legacy propagation vectors retain their existing allocation
contract; this is not a claim that all LR storage or RSS is budgeted.

contained-label goto paths. The final fast path therefore proves completed FIRST
and disjoint terminal labels in every state; overlapping labels use the original
closure algorithm. No oracle expectation changed. lr_work.tower selects the same
safe path, builds its graph on the coordinator, then uses existing WorkGraph/
WorkPool solver/action jobs, private results, admission and ordered joins. Old
range closure workers remain intact. No eager worker-core optimization returned.

Implementation is confined to lr_analysis.tower::lr_range_merge_result. The old
loop restarted binary insertion for every source range, including duplicate
sets, and could shift/reallocate repeatedly while growing one union. The new
helper counts missing exact identities with a forward sorted walk, reserves the
existing destination once, and merges backward in place. Empty/self/subset cases
need no allocation; one incoming range retains binary insertion. Overflow and
allocation results still flow through lr_reserve_result; denial does not publish
a partial set or clear the first error. No new allocator, scratch/cache owner,
second grammar, guessed identity, threshold, noalias annotation or shared mutable
state. Actual callers were audited: serial FIRST (same descriptor or different
nonterminals), suffix scratch versus immutable FIRST, propagation node owners,
and worker-private FIRST/propagation results versus frozen inputs. Their vectors
are separately owned or the identical self descriptor, tested before growth.
No claim is made that existing raw LR vectors are newly budgeted by this change.

States/actions/provenance, incremental declaration boundaries, module/revision
identity and the disjoint-label guard/range-overlap closure fallback are unchanged.
The generic helper also serves existing worker algorithms without changing their
admission, dispatch or publication. No second optimization was attempted.

### L2 declaration-call discovery concern: current prerequisite rules it out (2026-11-23)

Bounded follow-up to accepted3a7f4b39. Started on clean main, no surviving owned
build, CLI PID32440; required ff-only/rebase-merges/autostash pull froze published
a3fbe0a4. No production Tower source changed. A1 constructor/IDE preparation and
other owners' implementations remain untouched. Earlier full48d791a8 acceptance
and later focused603fa60a adoption retain their exact source identities.

The proposed direct allocation-underflow is not reachable: the call loop pops
one DeclarationCallScan, keeps its allocation/capacity, and the nominal branch
re-pushes that same nonnull node before any other scan push. vector_reserve returns
true without allocation for that reclaimed slot. Sibling calls to the helper
only enqueue work; this is its only caller that subsequently indexes the last
entry. No sibling assumes an append succeeded by reading a scan slot.

There is a superficially more plausible semantic-error path: the spelling
function makes sem_type_identity_call's final OR true even if callable resolution
reports ambiguity. However its production caller runs after declaration discovery.
sem_declaration_dependencies uses the same roots and resolves templates/functions
first; sem_callable_visible checks the union of functions/templates/type-functions
for ambiguity regardless of the selected table. The failed discovery ticket is
finished unsuccessfully, and the checking query depends on it. This rules out the
late ambiguity for those frozen module/name indexes. The execute transition first
requires a resolved ordinary callee; alias roots retain their type role and child
query ownership. These continuations do not introduce an unchecked ambiguous
function spelling into this nominal-value branch.

Fallible token/identifier work in sem_call_uses_value and sem_identifier is followed
by the existing sem_ok check before the final callable resolutions. Unqualified
callable resolution otherwise only reads ownership/import links and name tables;
its only error construction is the ambiguity above. Qualified resolution may
allocate identifier text, but failed namespace resolution returns null and failed
field decoding cannot find a named callable; qualified spelling is not function.
Thus an allocation denial cannot turn that final result into true on this path.
No mock failed context or manually emptied scan was used to bypass these guards.
No defensive runtime change is claimed necessary for the audited current chain.

Root cause: sem_run admitted only its immediate call/expression statements
through sem_module_expression. sem_defer_register checks the deferred prototype
through sem_statement, outside that outer list. The legacy immediate call path
then enters sem_call_specialization/sem_header with an unprepared substituted
stack(T)* parameter. stack is an ordinary executed type-producing template, not
a static type_functions entry; sem_type_call consequently reports Unknown type
constructor. Module ownership was intact; changing name lookup or classifying
stack as a static constructor would bypass the actual signature dependency.

no active declaration subjects, entity stage or query-read collector. Workers
and active query continuations keep their existing preparation/suspension path.

frame, deferring/loop state and scratch ownership survive the join. The ordinary
query graph prepares the signature/constructor before the statement publishes;
its expression is consumed once, and existing defer finish/clone/emit contracts
retain execution order. No recursive worker completion, alternate alias registry,

Concrete remaining boundary for ROOT: compiler-worker-group suppresses queued
messages after closure but its error listener only calls idempotent close.
A coordinator startup error queued before cancellation can reach its old caller
after replacement. Engine and LanguageService unconditionally stop their current
worker in that old callback, terminating the replacement and rejecting its work.
The HTML worker-processing/termination algorithms support this outside-global
error-task interleaving; this review did not reproduce it in Chromium. Caller
weakness predates the helper. Smallest proposed control retires A, installs B,
then delivers an ErrorEvent to A and checks that B survives. That checks the
transport boundary, not native task timing. Preserve active errors: the helper
intentionally closes before forwarding child failure, so an unconditional closed
error filter would hide a real failure. No overlapping transport patch made.

### 2026-11-24 proposal - staged grammar tables and bounded parser specialization

User idea, recorded as a proposal only: use ordinary Tower compile-time evaluation to read known grammar definitions and compute regex/DFA/LR artifacts; specialize the ordinary parsing algorithm against those known values so character ranges, transitions and grammar choices can become constants in generated code. Bundle versions for Bedrock/Foundation/Tower with the compiler. When grammar inputs differ, immediately use the current dynamic grammar/table path; potentially build an optimized replacement asynchronously and publish it once ready. User explicitly raised code size, peak memory, batching, dependency invalidation and repeated recompilation concerns. This entry authorizes no implementation, new executable-memory dependency or expansion of current release acceptance. Existing B1 regression repair and A2 bounded cold-construction task continue unchanged.

Assessment: promising, especially avoiding repeat cold grammar construction, but split construction savings from parsing throughput. Three independent tiers deserve measurement:
1. Build-time evaluation and packaging of validated immutable grammar/table data, interpreted by the existing compiled table engine. Potentially removes LR/DFA construction and temporary allocation on every cold process without multiplying parser machine code. Loading, identity checks, entity reconstruction and source/capture binding still cost time; unchanged grammar bytes alone do not justify skipping semantic dependencies or effects.
2. Ahead-of-time specialization of selected stable lexer/parser kernels against those tables. Character-class tests, fixed transitions and action dispatch may become direct code; ordinary backend optimization can then simplify it. Retain shared/table-driven cold or large states and common helper bodies rather than unrolling all states/rules. Bound generated bytes, compilation work and retained state.
3. Optional background specialization for long-lived editor/server workloads, only when expected remaining use amortizes compilation. A one-shot CLI may exit before any benefit. Bundled AOT artifacts amortize work across invocations; edited grammars can remain entirely table-driven.

Static table construction is not automatic partial evaluation of the parser. For table[state][input], state and input remain dynamic even when the table is constant. General constant propagation cannot simply erase that lookup. Residualization must preserve dynamic operations and may specialize control flow by state, using the ordinary Tower semantic graph/lowering rather than a separate constant evaluator or hand-maintained parser implementation. No template language is inherently required. The grammar can be an ordinary value known at one stage, with input supplied at a later stage; existing known-value/comptime support does not by itself prove an arbitrary general partial evaluator is implemented.

Current source inspected at329eb286c7 (runtimebf9429d9): syntax_baselines.tower stores world-owned source/revision baselines and bounded ParserStructureCache entries; parser_structure.tower shares frozen numeric LR structures only under matching world/budget/profile and exact structural fields, retaining per-version emission, captures, userdata and provenance. It is not an on-disk or embedded cross-process grammar cache. lr_runtime_specialize currently recognizes one nonempty terminal-only root production, preserves LR state/error correspondence and builds a sequence representation; it does not generate arbitrary native parser machine code. syntax_baseline_install still executes ordinary ordered parsing/validation/publication. Existing prior evidence locates material cold cost in Foundation/Tower grammar construction; historical startup47.7ms Foundation and selected-emission116->77 table calls are attribution at their own sources, not a forecast of this proposal's gains.

Correctness and representation:
- Keep Foundation as canonical semantic interchange and world-owned grammar entities authoritative. Persisted tables/code are disposable versioned derived execution artifacts with full source/build provenance, not a new authoritative grammar/AST. Use stable numeric IDs/offsets and explicit world reconstruction/rebinding, never serialized process pointers or foreign-world handles. Immutable mapped data may share storage only under an explicit ownership/accounting contract.
- Key reuse on the complete relevant dependency closure: grammar/import content and declaration order, seed and active-prefix identity, token/literal/reserved-name/regex encoding policy, captures/actions and any grammar-building compile-time inputs/effects; compiler semantic/representation version and applicable target/profile/ABI. Hashes index candidates; validate the complete contract/correspondence before use. Source coordinates/bindings stay revision-correct even when numeric automata can be reused.
- Every file still starts from its Bedrock seed and applies declarations after their boundaries. A final Tower parser cannot silently parse earlier prefixes, changed imports, overrides or malformed active grammar as if the final grammar had always existed. An accepted cached installation can replace execution only if its complete ordered semantic result/dependencies/effects are equivalent; otherwise retain the ordinary path. Baseline checkpoints and unchanged substructures may be useful without caching every transient revision.
- Runtime fallback means constructing the correct current grammar and using the existing table-driven engine, not reusing an obsolete grammar or necessarily interpreting Tower source one instruction at a time. Invalid grammar remains an actionable error. Cache misses or deliberately declining an optional optimization are distinct from a build/validation failure; preserve failure diagnostics.

Scheduling/invalidation proposal: represent artifact generation as shared CompilerWork/WorkGraph producers with frozen input revision/profile tickets and explicit memory/worker budgets. Deduplicate one in-flight build per semantic key across compilation units; prioritize foreground compilation, bound queued generations and coalesce obsolete optimization requests without coalescing away semantic declaration boundaries. FIRST/FOLLOW, nullability, lookahead propagation, lexical priority and conflicts can cross rule boundaries: do not assume changing one rule permits recompiling only that rule. Initially rebuild the affected automaton; finer dependency/SCC reuse needs proof and measurement. Cancellation joins owned work before releasing inputs.

Publish a complete immutable result through the coordinator after checking its original ticket and current desired key. Discard stale generations; keep old artifacts pinned until current readers finish. New parse requests or proved compatible construct boundaries may select the replacement. Do not change the automaton under a live LR stack, cursor, diagnostic context or lease merely because a background compilation finished. Both paths must produce identical tokens/trees/canonical output, errors/positions, effect order and ownership cleanup. Preserve the portable interpreter/no-required-guest-JIT contract. Embedded native/Wasm AOT is compatible in principle; arbitrary dynamic native code loading or browser compilation needs a separately explicit supported host capability and resource/lifetime design, never a mandatory baseline.

Performance hypotheses and experiment order:
- First compare current cold dynamic construction versus validated cached tables for identical bundled and edited grammars. Record initialization/validation/load time, parsing time and end-to-end compilation separately, small/large input, serial/profitable workers, cold/warm filesystem and repeated-world use.
- Then compare a bounded specialized lexer/hot parser kernel against the same tables. Record wall/CPU, backend generation/optimization/link time, code/data/package bytes, peak and retained RSS/charged storage, allocation traffic, branch behavior and instruction/data-cache misses where counters are available. Compiler IR, old tables, new tables/code and active readers may coexist; background work competes for the same cores/cache/bandwidth. Read-only packed tables could save memory; giant direct code could lose locality. Neither outcome is assumed.
- A rough necessary break-even condition is expected remaining parses * (table parse time - specialized parse time) > specialization/load/publication cost, with separate peak-memory/code-size limits and foreground interference accounted for. If parsing is a small fraction of compilation, even a large parser-only speedup has a limited end-to-end effect. Do not double-count saved construction and parser throughput.
- Differential tests use the ordinary table engine plus existing independent eager grammar oracles, complete output/diagnostic comparison, malformed/boundary Unicode/range/EOF cases, import/override/edit/revert cycles, stale async completion, forced failures, real concurrent readers and cancellation/drain. No full interpreter rewrite or per-edit optimized rebuild before a measured useful first tier.

Primary sources consulted2026-11-24: [re2c overview](https://re2c.org/) describes DFA generation as direct-coded lexers, providing a concrete precedent for specialized transitions; [re2c manual](https://re2c.org/manual/manual_c.html) documents alternative branch/table representations and code-generation tradeoffs. [Yallop, Xie and Krishnaswami, flap (PLDI2023)](https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~jdy22/papers/flap-a-deterministic-parser-with-fused-lexing.pdf) demonstrates staged specialized/fused parsing under its own deterministic grammar contract; its benchmark gains do not predict Tower LR/IDE results, and discarding token materialization is not automatically valid for Tower's observable token entities. [regex-automata lazy DFA documentation](https://docs.rs/regex-automata/latest/regex_automata/hybrid/index.html) describes demand-built states and bounded caches, including cache-reset costs; [full DFA documentation](https://docs.rs/regex-automata/latest/regex_automata/dfa/index.html) records potential exponential construction size for some regexes. These are algorithm/design precedents, not dependencies to introduce or reasons to reimplement Tower in another language.

Decision: journal the full vision and prefer a measured cached-table experiment before broad machine-code specialization or asynchronous compilation. Likely useful for stable bundled grammars; selective specialization is plausible; compile-every-revision/unroll-every-state is likely counterproductive without usage and size budgets. No new performance result, implemented feature or release promise follows from this proposal. Documentation-only work needs no runtime benchmark; prior measurements stay source-bound. Preserve existing journal bytes/todo and publish via the established unchanged-asset atomic process.


### 2026-11-24 desired language direction - general specialization and resumable stages

User clarified the parser idea is one application of a broader capability they strongly want: automatic specialization of ordinary Tower computations using any presently known values, including whole structs, available at build time and at later runtime/eval/compilation stages, potentially from any point in a program. They recalled an Emscripten optimization that runs code until an unavailable operation then preserves state. This discussion establishes desired language direction; general partial evaluation, arbitrary continuation capture and new syntax are not claimed implemented. Existing ECS performance owners continue their bounded assignments.

Identification correction: the Emscripten detail matches [EVAL_CTORS](https://emscripten.org/docs/optimizing/Optimizing-Code.html#eval-ctors), using [Binaryen wasm-ctor-eval](https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/blob/main/README.md#wasm-ctor-eval), more closely than Wizer. It can pre-execute constructors or portions of main, preserve resulting memory/globals and rewrite the remaining code. Its [implementation](https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/blob/main/src/tools/wasm-ctor-eval.cpp) serializes locals into entry assignments after successful chunks and retains a residual function. The inspected source explicitly limits partial progress to supported top-level block chunks and has a TODO for arbitrary-function partial evaluation: this is not an arbitrary live CPU-stack snapshot mechanism. Unknown imported operations can stop progress; ignore-external-input mode is an explicit changed assumption, not a policy Tower should silently adopt.

Related [Wizer](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wizer) runs a designated initializer and embeds resulting globals/nonzero memory; its normal contract is not automatically suspending any program at its first external call. [weval](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/weval) consumes a snapshot and recorded function-specialization requests, adds specialized functions and fills their references. Its [API](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/weval/blob/main/include/weval.h) distinguishes dynamic arguments, scalar constants and constant memory buffers, so aggregate known data is relevant. [Chris Fallin's explanation](https://cfallin.org/blog/2024/08/28/weval/) shows why context-sensitive specialization and reconverging control flow are needed beyond ordinary constant propagation. These are related mechanisms with different scope, not interchangeable implementations or a claim that Tower can already do all of them.

Proposed unified model:
- Ordinary evaluation with enough available inputs computes values/state. Pre-initialization packages the useful resulting state and remaining entry computation.
- Partial evaluation with a mixture of known/unknown inputs computes whatever is determined and constructs residual ordinary code for the rest. An unknown input need not end all optimization: preserve that operation and dynamic branch, then simplify independent known expressions without executing or reordering effects. Join control-flow contexts and memoize recurrence instead of unbounded path expansion.
- Runtime specialization runs that same compiler service at a later stage, when additional values have become available. A value unknown when the application was built may be known when a schema, grammar, ECS query or material arrives. Explicit eval executes; specialization produces a program that still accepts its remaining inputs. A backend may compile that residual program where supported, while the ordinary portable interpreter remains available.
- A known whole struct is ordinary typed data, not a second template language. Track knownness per field and through nested values/owned graphs: known mode/range/layout can remove branches or address calculations while unknown buffers/positions remain parameters. Mutable local work during evaluation can be valid; captured input lifetime and later writes/aliases determine which observations can remain constants. A known pointer address does not establish known stable pointee contents.

For example, specializing an ordinary operation against a configuration with known mode and sample count can remove mode dispatch and optionally unroll a bounded loop, leaving image/data inputs dynamic. The same mechanism can specialize parse(grammar, text), an ECS query against a stable archetype/component access plan, or a serializer against a known schema. It must not specialize against each changing entity value by default. No automatic noalias follows from known layouts; actual alias/access proofs remain required.

Any-point execution requires a semantic continuation, not only a memory image: remaining control flow, live locals and reachable owned state, pending effects/dependencies, target/profile, lifetimes/cleanup and any suspended calls. A compiler can lower an explicit source boundary into a residual callable plus captured environment; dead locals/allocations need not survive. Capturing an arbitrary optimized native instruction, foreign call or concurrently mutating world is a substantially stronger contract than a Tower source-level staging boundary. Preserve pointer/handle graph identity through relocatable typed reconstruction, not host stack addresses. External runtime resources require explicit reinitialization/capability bindings. Effects already performed must not replay; effects deferred must retain their order and happen with the intended multiplicity for each invocation. State cloning versus shared identity must be explicit.

Tower integration should reuse the same Foundation operations/interpreter semantics, world-owned entities, staged value and dependency queries, explicit lexical continuations and compiler work graph. Extend evaluation with well-defined residual dynamic operations and typed staged values; do not introduce a separate arithmetic/constant-folding semantics or a shadow authoritative IR. Work items carry source/revision/target/profile and observed input identity, owned scratch and generated artifact handles. Reuse/invalidation includes writes/escapes and external observations, including absence where relevant. Future guarded mutable specializations need atomic/versioned validity and a correct fallback, not a racy guard followed by unprotected reads. Frozen owned captures are a simpler initial contract.

Syntax decision requested by user: no new grammar syntax is required for an initial useful implementation. Prefer an ordinary typed compiler/library API conceptually mapping specialize(function, known_bindings, policy) to an owned typed artifact/callable for remaining inputs. This notation is illustrative, not a currently implemented Tower signature. Explicit frozen values, remaining-input descriptors and budgets can be ordinary values; infer known fields automatically when sound. Existing comptime can require that an eligible specialization request execute in the current compile stage, while the same service can run later with compilation capability. Preserve comptime's defined evaluate-now/error behavior; it must not silently become an unknown-value placeholder.

No-new-syntax does not mean a pure library can implement this with no compiler work: residualization, function/body inspection, inferred remaining signatures, constant-graph materialization and continuation capture require compiler services and contracts. Current typed function values are noncapturing; do not pretend a returned bare function pointer safely owns a captured heap. Start with an explicit owned compiled-artifact/environment and typed invocation contract. Later ergonomic syntax for selecting known fields, capturing a lexical environment or staging the remainder at a source boundary is optional sugar over these semantics. An ordinary compiler-recognized operation can initially mark a boundary; any new syntax must follow publish-before-adoption. Do not add a keyword simply to name an API.

Cost policy is part of making this practical: bound evaluation steps, specialized contexts, generated code/data, peak simultaneous old/new state and queued jobs; share artifacts by semantic key and prioritize foreground work. Retain useful generic residual loops rather than fully unrolling dynamic/infinite or excessively large static computations. Mandatory staging diagnoses an inability to satisfy its contract; optional specialization can explicitly retain correct generic execution while reporting failures according to policy. No hidden error suppression or silent change to user-required staging.

Implementation progression proposed, not scheduled as completed work: (1) typed whole/partial aggregate and graph known-value representation with effect/ownership rules; (2) function-boundary residualization with static/dynamic arguments and canonical Foundation round-trip; (3) measured parser/schema/ECS-plan consumers; (4) explicit resumable source boundaries and owned state materialization; (5) supported runtime compilation/publication with shared budgets, invalidation and stale-ticket rejection. Differential original-versus-residual execution must cover targets/engines, aggregate alias/identity, partial unknown branches/loops, effects and once-only replay, mutation/invalidation, failure/cancellation and bounded memory/code growth. Existing query continuations are groundwork, not proof that these general facilities exist.

Current docs inspected: tower.md's intended arbitrary staged values, foundation.md's combined compiler/runtime model, function-values.md's noncapturing ownership contract, attributes.md's supported staged struct results and computed-type-arguments.md's aggregate/capture continuations. Scalar-only historical wording in tower.md does not override those later aggregate receipts. A whole-struct comptime result is still distinct from specializing an arbitrary computation against partially known struct fields. This note records the broader requested direction and API-first syntax choice; no production/compiler/syntax edit or new runtime performance claim. ### 2026-11-24 clarification - comptime is a stage requirement, not an aggressive-specialization request

User explicitly asked to keep each concept separate and avoid overloading comptime, relating specialization to shader branch elimination/inlining/unrolling. Decision: share compiler/interpreter infrastructure but expose distinct composable contracts. Evaluation yields a value; comptime requires that evaluation at the current compilation stage; specialization yields residual ordinary code for remaining inputs; compilation targets an executable representation; pre-initialization/snapshot retains state plus a remaining entry; optimization policy controls transformation effort/code growth. Asynchronous scheduling is orthogonal and uses existing work handles. These operations are adjacent and may compose, rather than mutually exclusive meanings of one keyword.

Examples in prose to avoid implying unimplemented API syntax: comptime applied to an ordinary grammar builder requests the grammar/table value. Specializing an ordinary parser against that known value requests a remaining parser accepting input text. Requiring the specialization request itself to run at compile time is an explicit composition. The same specialization may run later when runtime configuration arrives. A whole-struct comptime value does not by itself request separate functions for every consumer or all possible struct values. Automatic knownness inference and ordinary profitable optimization may use it without changing that semantic distinction.

Do not promise maximum inlining, zero dynamic branches or full unrolling from either operation. The specialization contract is equivalence under fixed bindings with the remaining inputs dynamic; budgets and optimization quality are separate. Preserve loops or shared generic helpers where expansion would be unprofitable. Required staging failure remains an error; optional optimization can retain a correct residual operation under an explicit reported policy. Ordinary shader uniformity means invocations share a value, not that its value was known when machine code was compiled.

Primary analogy: [Khronos specialization-constant sample](https://docs.vulkan.org/samples/latest/samples/performance/specialization_constants/README.html) distinguishes values supplied before pipeline compilation from uniform-buffer/push values supplied afterward; knowing the former can permit branch removal and unrolling. [HLSL loop attributes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-for) separately expose loop/unroll/compile-effort controls, and [branch attributes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-if) distinguish branch from flatten. These are precedents for separating known bindings from optimization strategy, not a blanket branchless-shader claim or Tower syntax to copy.

Added a clearly proposed separation table to docs/tower.md so this decision is discoverable outside the long journal. Initial API-first approach remains; possible later capture/continuation syntax must express its own operation and follow publish-before-adoption. No new keyword or production behavior in this turn. D1's publishedc31d2d82 native-package peer was independently read/ACKed and handoff updated; its actual5 relocation controls and exact artifacts close that gate, while B1 performance repair/A2 cold work and publication remain distinct. Documentation-only validation is contract/link/diff review plus atomic unchanged-asset publication; runtime profiling is inapplicable.

## 2026-11-24 · Slot 8 · Bounded growth of private-stage descriptor pages

Frozen baseline `c7e3e091aa15db30ff9edd6dcb2a3ab465bb79ef`, tree `a81ba6dcb22af49b91201843d4045048d0abf8be`. The earlier dense-unit result identified a doubling of the separately allocated grant ledger. This trial changed only the row limit passed for a new private-stage Entity descriptor page. The allocator still looks up an available page by type and stride before reserving a new one, applies its byte ceiling, and transfers existing pages intact on publication. The stage already owns the count of its successfully staged nodes.

The first trial took its limit from the stage node index capacity, bounded to 8–32. The x64 byte ceiling gave successive actual capacities of 8, 16 and 19. Dense joined charge rose 153,633 B, but 2,049 fewer live grants avoided 5,242,880 B of ledger capacity. Four small units cost an additional 9,096 charged bytes. An observation of actual successful publications found 1,024 stages with 33 nodes and 1,025 with eight on the dense input. The 33-node stages used three pages holding 43 slots. Replaced this trial with one doubling, from eight to sixteen requested rows after eight nodes. It serves 33 nodes with the same three grants and 40 slots. Both policies reuse partial pages and preserve the existing allocator's refusal path. The raw trials, including the superseded progression, remain in the lane packet.

**Measured result.** Retain the 8→16 policy. On a 1,024-body unit it reduced joined charge by 485,343 B and separately allocated ledger capacity by 5,242,880 B at both worker widths. That saves **5,728,223 B (4.94%)** on the specified combined measure. Four 16-body units saved a further **30,840 B** and 136 grants versus fixed-eight, bringing the saving over the earlier ordinary store-sized pages to 326,036 charged bytes. The grant counts below describe outstanding reservations after join. Ledger capacity is entries capacity times entry size; the separately sampled physical RSS need not move by the same amount.

**Useful work.** A third, separately built Tower probe counted actual payloads claimed in each threaded batch. Its decoder checked all admitted callbacks and payload totals at each join. At jobs 4 the small input dispatched 529 payloads in 151 threaded batches with 249 peer callbacks. The singleton peers claimed 290 payloads on 24–27 and 10 on 0–3. On 0–3, 246 of the 249 callbacks claimed zero, and 149 of 151 batches finished with all payloads executed by the caller. The previous LR producer yielded 292 and zero peer payloads on the two masks. The large workload had 5,449 payloads and 294 callbacks. On 0–3 only 9 singleton and 17 baseline callbacks did any work. Those callbacks claimed 151 and 3,494 payloads, respectively. A few large batches make callback counts a poor throughput proxy. These counts are individual observations with probes enabled. The ordinary timings above remain the performance comparison.

**Decision.** Retain the singleton lookup. Of the 151 small-input threaded batches, 130 held two or three payloads. In the quieter phase trace, 126 of these began inside an LR table build (70 with two payloads and 56 with three). Compare caller-only execution for those 126 LR batches against the current handoff on quiet and loaded CPUs, preserving the larger batches as controls. Measure actual payload cost and claims before proposing a shared threshold. On quiet CPUs workers claimed real work, yet the small and large ordinary invocations consumed 74 and 94 ms more CPU on average and both finished later. The saturated host's extra second cannot establish a universal compiler cost.

The 64 ordinary compiles had zero major faults or new quota throttles and peaked at 165,520 KiB process RSS. The shared cgroup high-water mark was 11,111,735,296 bytes under a 57,954,795,520-byte limit. Packet `cd1704db-9339-4f4e-8d5f-1352646c4d26.tar.gz` includes the individual samples, raw host/phase/scheduler records, full compiler packages, canonical objects, linked programs, diagnostic source and failures. Initial diagnostic builds rejected a conflicting clock declaration, a late import and a missing getenv declaration. The first decoder build caught an extra pointer indirection. Corrected readers rejected deliberate truncated/incomplete controls. The private release ELF, complete resources and compiler sources were restored and compared successfully. The tracked change is this journal entry.

Host 3 assignment `8d857df2-7a38-451d-8b93-4a097349975d` used integrated main `add73163fa32aa0c444dcba60bd5bdb1ab39db34`, tree `ac778c28263ad0690886691a87d170349e5d4602`. The integrated default Release ELF was `f1caff1c2e399fb306da459a5caa12e79e68428ab27783d911171e2fc480ba3b`. All three timing arms used its complete 55-file runtime resource tree, the checked-in Linux x64 bootstrap and the same entry object. The production package used Clang/LLVM 19.1.7, build parallelism 2 and compiler jobs 1.

A separate checked jobs-4 trace on the 16-function input identified 70 two-payload LR dispatches (5 FIRST, 21 action, 23 propagation and 21 runtime row), 56 three-payload dispatches (19 action, 18 propagation and 19 runtime row) and 8 wider dispatches. Both patches changed only those four producers' calls to `compiler_kernel_dispatch_admitted_result`. The two-payload arm passed zero extra lanes for at most two payloads. The next arm extended just that cutoff to three. The existing entry validation, admission, graph tickets, private scratch, caller loop, error handling and ordered publication were used. All wider dispatches kept their requested lanes.

The initial two-payload proof ran baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline on the quiet set. It took 341/356/357/360 ms. The full comparison used fresh processes with warm filesystem pages and no observer. Each CPU mask and input had six balanced blocks, with every arm and worker width in every block. The observer shell was pinned to CPU 60. On the 32-core EPYC 7542, CPUs 24–27 were 0.7–4.7% busy before the run and CPUs 0–3 were 100% busy. These are distinct physical cores within each set. Every comparison used a single fixed set, and separate process checks confirmed both requested masks. The effective cgroup covered CPUs 0–63, with quota 1,228,800 µs per 100,000 µs. The host was shared.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Quiet, 16 | 302 / 304 / 304 | 356 / 354 / 337 | 386 / 377 / 344 |
| Quiet, 1000 | 552 / 555 / 549 | 583 / 596 / 581 | 635 / 644 / 614 |
| Saturated, 16 | 344 / 349 / 343 | 1385 / 933 / 656 | 367 / 365 / 358 |

On quiet CPUs, the two-payload cutoff slowed all six large jobs-4 pairs by 11–16 ms. Extending it to three recovered that cost. Against baseline, the three-payload cutoff saved 8–25 ms for the small input, while the large paired differences ranged from 11 ms faster to 9 ms slower. On saturated CPUs both increments improved every jobs-4 pair, with combined mean savings of 729 and 702 ms. The mean small jobs-4 voluntary switches fell from 472 to 133 on quiet CPUs and from 424 to 118 on busy CPUs. All 144 ordinary objects matched both the frozen 904-byte reference and the new serial object. The linked executables also matched serial byte-for-byte and printed exactly `15\n` or `999\n` with exit zero. Maximum RSS was 164,876 KiB, shared peak charge 11,787,845,632 bytes under a 57,954,795,520-byte cap, and no measured run added a quota throttle or major fault. The ordinary CLI creates its explicit-worker world without a Tower budget.

The unmodified retained-source fixture observed two concurrent LR kernels on baseline with two workers. Both cutoffs exited 1 on its real-overlap assertion. At width two, the action and propagation kernels monitored by that fixture always fit the caller-only cutoff. The failure reproduced after all exact output and edit/retry checks preceding the assertion. A separate copy of the identical retained-workload body at width four observed four kernels active together for each arm. Each finite ledger reached 75,581,223 charged bytes and finished with zero live owners and zero charged bytes. The original bounded LR refusal/retry, worker equivalence, scratch budget, LR order oracle (150 randomized trials) and dependency permutations passed for all three arms. Every deliberate wrong-result permutation returned 1 with actual 1112 and wanted 1113.

**Decision.** Reject both unconditional payload cutoffs and retain the current implementation. A count of two can represent a fully utilized two-worker request. A future experiment can distinguish a batch that fills its requested worker width from an underfilled batch on a four-worker request. The stock two-worker overlap assertion and the quiet 1000-function pairs provide independent acceptance checks. The private production package and source were restored and matched byte-for-byte. The tested patches, ELFs, resource tree, individual timings, comparisons and failing controls are in the assignment packet. Only this journal entry is committed.

The manager independently ran all 144 linked programs from the cutoff experiment and compared each object against the corresponding serial reference. On the manager's two eligible CPUs, the archived baseline passed the unmodified retained-source case and observed two overlapping LR kernels. Both candidate executables exited 1 at the overlap assertion, with the same complete streams as on the producer. The four-worker positive controls in the packet each observed four simultaneous kernels. Both unconditional cutoffs were rejected. A separate same-host trial will test whether an underfilled batch can use the caller while retaining full-width handoff.
