**The shared budget gate accounts for most of the measured wall penalty of widening from four to 30.** An AB/BA private experiment changed only the gate used by this batch’s existing reservation ledger, from its glibc adaptive mutex to a process-private pthread spin lock. Both arms used the same ELF, the production allocator and the same ledger code, capacity, receipts, lane scheduling and twelve input worlds. At four workers the four-pair mean changed from 2.481 to 2.199 s wall and 9.586 to 8.611 s CPU. At 16 it changed from 3.239 to 2.264 s and 37.698 to 23.929 s. At 30 it changed from 3.259 to 2.312 s and 41.688 to 27.193 s. At 30 all four wall improvements lay between 26.4% and 31.5%. The four-to-30 wall penalty shrank from 0.778 to 0.113 s (85.5%). The CPU penalty shrank from 32.102 to 18.582 s (42.1%). The serial control has no gate and averaged 4.166 and 4.175 s. The stock and private mutex timing series have distinct ELF identities.

At 30 the gate substitution lowered mean voluntary switches in the frontend interval from 970,125 to 11,977 and whole-process system time from 24.765 to 1.845 s. It increased whole-process user time as workers spun. Both arms had 12 overlapping units. Separate grammar traces executed 34,980 semantic payloads in 1,992 dispatches in either arm. The mutex/spin traces observed within-dispatch semantic peaks of 19/29 and action peaks of 4/4, with 492/455 action waves. The gate change can alter when nested work obtains lanes and how transient allocations overlap. At 30 its maximum explicit charge changed from 852,146,404 to 690,726,025 bytes while maximum whole-process RSS changed from 1,225,048 to 1,229,632 KiB. Both held 373,980,856 charged bytes and 251,555 grants at join. These results identify a synchronization cost on this allocation. They establish neither a production spin policy nor a portable improvement on oversubscribed hosts.

**Bounded attribution.** In the stock interval, 23.328 of the 30.996 additional CPU seconds from four to 30 fell inside the outer unit callbacks on their executing threads. A separate private Tower probe sampled one pseudorandom position in each block of 256 complete shared-budget transactions on those threads. Both clocks ran outside the lock. The summed interval includes acquisition, protected ledger work and release. The outer-thread count fell from 4.322 million transactions at four to 3.852 million at 30. Across two opposite-order runs, the raw extrapolated thread CPU means were 9.150 and 33.191 s. Subtracting the same run's empty clock-pair cost gave approximately 6.205 and 30.560 s (8/16 workers gave 15.580/30.967 s). The delta localizes the growing cost to these transactions. Different diagnostic and stock schedules, extrapolation, probe overhead and post-join clock calibration limit exact percentage attribution. Nested workers outside the outer callbacks are excluded. The clocks cannot split spinning, cache-line movement, kernel entry and protected accounting.

An initial probe timed lock and unlock separately. Reading clocks while holding the mutex inflated the expanded estimates, so those values were excluded from the attribution. One shell setup error and five failed diagnostic builds were retained and the public compiler accepted the corrected private probe. A GNU clock-profile cross-check produced four empty profiles with “itimer could not be set”. All four workload processes passed their output checks, but they supplied zero PC-sampling evidence.

The stock runs observed outer peaks of 1/4/8/12/12 and mean active outer units of 1.00/3.93/6.80/11.64/11.71 at widths 1/4/8/16/30. A separate interval trace at those widths observed within-dispatch semantic peaks of 1/2/7/7/19. Cross-world frontend parse and semantic-run intervals overlapped for 0/173/208/166/0 ms respectively. At 30 up to twelve parses overlapped, followed by up to ten semantic runs. The phases' independent peaks are not additive. A sampled wide run used all 30 selected logical CPUs. The native `parser_structure_reuse.tower` fixture publishes A for `Root -> Term -> 'x'`, opens a capture-distinct hit, and replaces A with B for `'y'` in a limit-one cache. It checks the slot identity, B's two owners (table and cache), and A's reference counts of three, two and one through hit, eviction and original-table close. State zero in the surviving alias borrows the structure's charged buffer and has one kernel and three ordered context positions. The productions are 0, 1 and 2, each at term zero. Only the final position is terminal, with both bounds equal to 'x'. The rule lookup returns 1 and parsing x exposes the alias's private capture. The existing table-owner closure fixture supplies the independent row and rule reference.

A separate one-lane ledger watches the table during the real build. Once the descriptor and context buffer have transferred, the optional index takes its first growth grant. The serial budget gate arms the existing one-shot physical allocation fault on leaving this grant. This avoids hardcoding an allocation ordinal or adding a compiler hook. The table builds with one reference and a usable context and runtime. The empty cache owns no entry or reservation. An equivalent fresh table subsequently publishes to the same cache with two references, then parses with its own capture after the uncached table retires. After closing all owners, live grants, used bytes and used lanes equal the initial zero snapshot and the physical buffer count equals its baseline.

It does not call an additional row wrapper on the ungated path. In two reversed fixed-core diagnostic pairs, stock retired 21,026 published rows across 79 runtimes before join. The two owning row-vector publication sites are the ordinary constructor and the coordinator publishing joined worker results. ### Host 4 · Close joined multi-unit owners before the runtime compiler starts

Receipt `cb46a7db-8d90-4a90-937b-737aadddef6c` compares the ordinary Ubuntu
LLVM 19.1.1 package from source `902a358f`, checked-in pin `217f0631`,
with a clean default-pin build changing the driver only. Both input archives
and all ten requested members matched their recipient SHA-256 values. The
earlier `24752653` measurements used a different compiler. This comparison
reuses its 13-unit invoice, four physical cores and /proc sampler.

After the join the driver still needs the unit worlds for diagnostics, semantic
function flags and dependency output. It copies import text and allocates each
export and input argument independently. Additional object files still have to
exist when the linker opens them. The entry source text belongs to DriverRequest.
The emitted entry object belongs to the backend LLVM memory buffer. Closing the
batch while retaining its byte pointer would leave a dangling linker input.

The driver now prepares the existing generated entry in the internal linker's
owned input table, or writes the external linker's existing temporary file.
It can then close the backend and its frontend lease, dispose the extra source
snapshots and run the runtime compiler. Temporary object files stay with the
driver until link return. Moving the generated table into the linker clears
the old owner. A runtime compiler failure releases the prepared table from
the link owner instead. The successful path adds no entry copy or temporary.
The existing linker allocation is outside WorkBudget in both builds. The
backend's length-based object reservation remains live until backend close.

The independent bounded four-slot check passed. A Chromium page owned the coordinator and four children and loaded the generated execution and thread worker assets from the respective sites. ### Jenkins build 3 on 448d61fe, aggregate parser fault fixture

Build 3 on 2026-11-25 ran both formatting CTests successfully in 3.82 s, confirming the build 2 fixture repair. The Clang 19.1.1 native core build linked all 48 actions. The aggregate parser CTest aborted at 2.67 s. The remaining 14 core tests passed, including the standalone LR analysis. The manager reported linux-1 online with two executors. The console ends the aggregate output at the ordinary LR item-graph checkpoint (12,664 live bytes, 1,048,576 peak). That checkpoint precedes teardown, and the aggregate continues to shared entity and registry tests. The log contains no failing assertion or stack trace.

Source inspection found a deterministic failure in the following shared entity fixture. Its first named attachment fills the parent's inline child index. Reattaching the same child by its borrowed name reserves a larger index and releases the old name into the pool. Replacing that child with another named "value" then needs neither index growth nor a fresh name allocation. The fixture armed the next physical allocation failure at that point and called a bare abort when replacement succeeded.

Checked the attachment sequence by invoking the existing 32-bit Tower exports through Node 24.22.1 WASI. The published tower.wasm SHA-256 is `5aa8f756d825308505431106baaefadcc0a3ef821807592a3de4e0e9de95155c`. Its recorded compiler source is 902a358f. The entity implementation and layouts, work budget and buffer sources compare byte-identically to 448d61fe. The minimal setup retained 38,343 bytes after first attachment and 38,447 after borrowed-name reattachment. With a competing reservation filling a 65,536-byte ledger, replacement before growth returned Capacity and preserved the child, borrowed name and parent links. Releasing the reservation allowed reattachment. Filling the ledger again still allowed replacement, on the same name page, with the old child detached. Store disposal returned the ledger to its pre-store baseline. This exercises the production capacity path. The build 3 log cannot independently identify the site of its native abort.

Moved the native injected failure before child-index growth and require the exact Memory result and preserved relationship. Retained borrowed-name reattachment and successful replacement. Shared entity checks now use the existing flushed test diagnostic. Compiler and allocator sources are unchanged. `git diff --check` passed. The native instrumented aggregate and complete pipeline rerun are pending on Jenkins after manager review. No runtime performance or sanitizer comparison was made for this fixture change.

## 2026-11-25 — Joined WASI pthread slot handoff on host 1

Assignment d3582cb6. The retained mandatory Node suite returned 2 at
lifecycle 80, the ordinary observer at 145, and the bounded delayed READY
publication at zero. On the verified 1c2cc042 checkout the delayed baseline
again failed at zero (grants four then one). The ordinary baseline completed
2,048 this time. The proposed fix binds each successful pthread_create to
its underlying JS worker and synchronizes successful pthread_join with that
specific worker’s final publication. Independent running handles keep
their slots. The existing Tower width and overlap assertions stay in force.

The implementation passes the address of the live Tower thread-handle cell
to two WASI host imports. The only spawning coordinator binds the cell after
successful creation and looks it up after successful join, before freeing it.
Reassigning a READY worker clears its previous binding. A late join for a
retired binding therefore cannot wait on its successor. The current binding
can wait on its own RUNNING word. The child publishes READY or its failure
and notifies that word without a coordinator message. An exhausted spawn
returns the WASI failure result immediately. Capacity still permits inline
execution when independent handles own the group.

WASI SDK 34.0 (wasi-libc 2e6fb9d8ee0c) disassembly puts the final
thread-list unlock and notify inside wasi_thread_start. pthread_join calls
the libc list synchronization. The subsequent JS READY store is outside
both operations. In the delayed trace, join for handle 70048 had already
returned with all four status words RUNNING. Only physical slot 0 changed
to READY before that handle was freed. Slots 1, 2 and 3 were acknowledged

### Contributor guidance for owned components and staged dependencies

The compiler audit traced two decisions a contributor can test in an ordinary
pass. Before choosing component storage, follow one entity from creation to
its last reader and identify who can publish a change. For staged reads,
record both the missing value and the query that produces it. The staged
alias fixture distinguishes a mutable binding's type from its value. The
retained import test identifies which results survive an edit. AGENTS.md
now asks contributors to exercise these cases and compare serial and
parallel outputs. This publication changes guidance only and reuses the
existing compiler and site assets.
[Staged alias fixture](../scaffolding/tests/staging_aliased_type.tower) ·
[Retained import test](../scaffolding/tests/execution_world.tower)

## Ordinary native CLI scaling on the 4a3aa2d6 candidate

The normal Linux x64 compiler built the same three single-source programs
using public `902a358f55e65a4582d50802204a83428971ad5d` and candidate
`4a3aa2d653ae7feb5e79d7b76c5a048ad741abf6`. Each program makes eight
compile-time calls. The long and chained forms execute the same number of
loop iterations and print the same nine integers. In the chained form each
successor needs its predecessor's result. The short form keeps the calls
independent and reduces the iterations per call from 32,768 to 128.

One AMD EPYC 7542 host ran a single timed process tree at a time. The compiler
and its children used logical CPUs 24–27 on four distinct physical cores. Its
cgroup admitted CPUs 0–63 with a quota of 12.288 CPUs. No timed row added a
throttled period. The cpuset was shared with other host services. Each fresh
compiler process used its own package resources, Ubuntu 24.04 under PRoot,
LLVM and Clang 19.1.1, and the same runtime IR and system link inputs. The
harness removed the output before each invocation and kept filesystem pages
warm. One warmup per setting preceded four scored blocks. At a fixed width
the packages ran immediately adjacent, with each package running first twice.

Candidate medians appear below. Each slash-separated column follows the jobs
order for its row. CPU is user plus system time. Individual peak RSS comes
from wait4. Tree RSS sums the compiler and Clang at each snapshot, typically
26 ms apart. Sampling can miss a short peak or count shared pages twice.
The speedup is the median of the four within-block one-worker/four-worker
wall ratios.

| Input and output | Jobs | Wall (ms) | CPU (ms) | Peak individual RSS (KiB) | Sampled peak tree RSS (KiB) | Paired speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Long independent, object | 1/2/4 | 1599/1078/905 | 1572/1672/1969 | 86840/90916/91856 | 80818/82136/81058 | 1.776× |
| Long independent, executable | 1/2/4 | 2014/1496/1330 | 1973/2083/2409 | 97050/97010/96828 | 181256/182896/184420 | 1.518× |
| Short independent, object | 1/4 | 314/425 | 287/427 | 86918/91638 | 79900/80568 | 0.740× |
| Short independent, executable | 1/4 | 741/841 | 697/831 | 97148/97148 | 179300/185752 | 0.870× |
| Equal-work chain, object | 1/4 | 1548/1675 | 1522/1669 | 86728/91856 | 79748/90956 | 0.921× |
| Equal-work chain, executable | 1/4 | 2008/2117 | 1967/2096 | 97284/97200 | 178884/185358 | 0.954× |

On both compilers the long independent input finished sooner at each
successive width in every scored block. On the other two inputs four workers
took longer in every block. Separate phase samples place some of the penalty
inside the interval that includes parsing and staged evaluation. The next
test is to identify which work in that interval incurs the excess before
changing worker admission.

At fixed width the candidate finished sooner in 55 of 56 pairs and used less
peak individual and sampled tree RSS in all 56. In the one reversed pair, a
four-worker long executable took 1342 ms on the candidate and 1287 ms on the
public package. Across four blocks for that setting, public to candidate
medians were 1462 to 1330 ms wall, 2586 to 2322 ms user CPU, 116 to 84 ms
system CPU, 142572 to 96828 KiB peak individual RSS, and 235028 to 184420
KiB sampled tree RSS. These are whole-package comparisons on this host.

The manager verified 1,601 member checksums, checked all 140 compiler rows
against raw process accounting, and recomputed 56 scored revision pairs and
80 within-release width comparisons. All 70 matrix guests exited zero with
the expected stdout bytes and empty stderr. Both releases and all measured
widths produced byte-identical objects and executables for each source.

## Checked generic inspection across declaration workers

When checked inspection at `be4bc2d6` published its temporary bindings to
source nodes, each annotation kept the private component kind alive. A
failed later phase could detach the kind from the document while leaving
its annotations on a declaration held by another owner. Checking the world
only after dropping that declaration concealed the bug.

Candidate `be41c755` copies the binding values into a budgeted work vector
while the document retains their syntax. It discards the first stage before
declaration workers run, leases the source nodes again, restores the values
and publishes after the last fallible walk. Two evaluation batch allocations
now return the typed memory error before acquiring a work ticket.

## Conflict precedence under a shared LR index budget

Release of candidate 4ede3fb9 is on hold. The duplicate-production fixture in lr_runtime_faults.tower has a shift row and a reduction row before the reduce/reduce conflict at state 2. On x64 the eight direct-index slots for those two rows need a 96-byte grant including the allocation header. If another unit leaves 95 bytes available after conflict selection, the serial and joined constructors can fail their final allocation. They destroy the private runtime and return null. The frontend then reports a resource failure in place of the selected conflict. The public baseline has already indexed its accepted rows when it selects the conflict. This is a source-derived ordering case. An executed reproduction under that exact schedule is pending.

The existing physical fault sweep accepts a null runtime with a memory error. The existing one-byte budget test exercises index construction without a grammar conflict. Together they leave the caller-visible diagnostic unchecked. The receiver is exercising the combined condition, access to prior valid states, retry and complete cleanup at native and Wasm widths. Receipt 2bb3d439 contains the frozen source comparisons and arithmetic. The manager verified its 71 checksums, all 60 ordinary driver rows against the original record, and the 23 wins in 24 measured pairs. Three of the four parallel comparisons recorded higher peak live budget use even though both serial limits improved. A separate four-worker valid-invoice test will check whether the increase affects admission under a fixed byte cap. No executable changed in this documentation update.

## Semantic work after an unrelated retained-source edit

At `2421c659`, a coordinator can keep a compiler world, module environment and
execution session alive through edits. The ordinary `execution_session_compile`
closes the preceding checked program before creating its successor.
`semantic_compile_budget` initializes an empty work graph and disposes the
semantic context before returning the checked program. Host 4 traced this
lifetime in the retained import diamond at one and two native workers.

The new test at `18b3beee` changes a separate producer from 71 to 73. Only
`choose(true)` requests its value. The evaluation of `choose(false)` requests
the right arm, the shared leaf and its forward-declared helper. The root
aggregate's declaration requests the left function's declaration, which in
turn requests the leaf seed's declaration for its return type. Replacing only
the shared leaf changes the aggregate size from 1 to 8, the staged result
from 25 to 45 and the seed from 7 to 19. An unknown type produces zero guest
steps and bytes. Repair gives size 2, staged result 65 and seed 9.

On the untouched repeat and unrelated edit, the same Tower, left and right
module snapshots supplied grammar entities. The shared leaf was cloned once
into each new request. The code-only side module was reparsed. Both requests
registered and completed 248 semantic tasks, issued 346 tickets and recorded
350 dependency edges. All 70 task subjects changed identity in the retained
world. The identical type prelude alone accounted for 114 tasks and 202
tickets. The failing request ended with 107 successful tasks, seven cancelled
and zero running. Fresh worlds agreed on every step's Foundation or diagnostic
and ordered guest bytes. The budget returned to zero bytes, live reservations
and lanes after close.

On a Ryzen 7 5800H, Ubuntu 24.04.5 and LLVM 19.1.1, CPUs 0,2,4,6, four
observer-free samples per arm gave the following third-request medians.
At one worker an untouched repeat took 17.76 ms wall and an unrelated edit
17.85 ms. At two workers they took 22.75 and 22.29 ms. Synchronized semantic
kernel observations reached width two. In separate probes, installing the
ordinary Tower grammar at byte 13 of the side module took 9.98 and 13.57 ms
on the edit, respectively. Each repeat and edit supplied the same ordered
109 rules, 296 alternative entities and 12 tokens. The whole timed call
outside the frontend parse phase took at most 2.84 and 3.15 ms in those
edit probes. The import parser belongs to the request's module graph and is
destroyed with it.

A bounded follow-up could lend the next import parser one immutable syntax
version for this transition, owned by the module environment and keyed by
the existing ordered grammar identities, world and Bedrock revision. Its

budget. This experiment changes the regression fixture only. The ordinary
selector passed, and a stale side producer made the new oracle exit 1.

### Jenkins 42 desktop continuous typing

Jenkins tested `0a67e17c47b601c884efaf97a1ee9a53ad7e5ab8`. The console
(SHA-256 `cc1ccb32b940f5efc1e94aa54bbb34789105c492176ab0d6f6875ab6b8b78bec`)
reports 513 Node passes, two skips, and a browser run with 239 passes, two
skips and one failure. The desktop typing test saw zero `Complete` status
mutations during a burst with a 15 ms key delay. Jenkins skipped archiving
after the failure. The supplied console has no per-edit worker timings.

Each edit advances the generation. The parser analyzes on an animation frame,
keeps one request in flight and coalesces pending edits. When another edit
overtakes a reply, `perform` drops that reply before rendering. The old test
required at least one reply to win this wall-clock race. On host 8 it passed
four ordinary desktop runs. Delaying only the real worker's outgoing messages
by 120 ms reproduced the exact zero count twice. In a separate instrumented
run the worker had already parsed five intermediate offsets (748, 757, 772,
780 and 788) at that zero count. After draining, the last offset was 794, the
whole comment had the expected highlighting, the worker had built zero grammar
tables in all six replies and no replacement parser worker had started.
This establishes a sufficient cause for the failure. Jenkins' actual delivery
latencies remain unknown.

The revised browser test advances the page clock one 16 ms frame after each
of three keyboard batches. It checks the exact highlighted comment at each
prefix before sending more input and checks all three real Wasm replies for
zero grammar builds. The adjacent slow-response test exercises edits that
overtake a reply. The change is confined to the browser test. Product runtime,
allocation and native sanitizer comparisons are inapplicable.

Host 8 used Debian 12 x86-64, Ryzen 9 7900X (12 cores, 24 logical CPUs,
affinity 0–23, 23.04-CPU quota), Node 24.22.3, Playwright 1.65.1 and Chromium
159.0.8154.6. The local loopback server used the published UI built at

manifest `f12b6bdff9c45758b1de334ee8bee3f1b3b86d7424f232242f069a8aa25ea6ef`.

## Lending the first imported grammar to a nested reader

The retained diamond at `da25567f` builds the ordinary Tower grammar at
byte 13 of `retained_side.tower`. Its 109 rule names, 296 ordered alternatives
and 12 tokens already occur in the root parser's session cache. That cache
retains the original build key and the compiled version. The nested reader
can take one reference in its existing active-version slot. Its graph owns
the idle import reader until another import resets it or the graph closes.
An active reader can also be the last owner after the root changes its active
grammar and discards its cache.

The loan is available for the first import in an ordinary reader in a bound
environment. Its resolved dependency must be the same grammar-bearing module
as the active root's first dependency in that same request graph. The lookup
checks the world, Bedrock revision, ordered rule names and each rule's ordered
alternative entities, followed by the ordered token entities. It reads the
bounded root index without updating recency. A miss goes through the reader's
ordinary installation. The change adds zero cache slots, heap buffers or
budget reservations and does not extend the root cache's lifetime.

A trial comparison of the packed allocation order missed the measured case.
`syntax_revision_create` sorts the rule views while leaving the underlying
storage in declaration order. Comparing the logical views recovered the hit.
A transparent wrapper exported the exact same entities from another path and
correctly missed. Editing a grammar behind an import alias rebuilt the root
version and changed the side and root effects from 17 to 19. The reader borrowed
the new identity. A shift/reduce conflict produced identical fresh and retained
diagnostics at byte 12 with no guest steps. Repair restored the original effects.
The lease fixture checked rejected admission, successful retry, reordered
alternatives and tokens, eviction with a suspended reader, and zero owners after
close. Cancellation joined two admitted unit workers that used the loan.

### Borrowed foreach on fixed-size arrays

A pointer to a fixed array carries an element type and a checked extent.
The frontend saves the source once, indexes into that array and advances the
cursor before the loop body can continue. The value form copies scalars and
pointers; the borrow form gives the body the address of its element. The
nominal collection protocol retains its own cleanup. A bare element pointer
still needs an explicit bound.

Host 5 compiled each substitution and both together in the real semantic unit. The candidate stores `GenericContext*`, `Entity*` and `EntityStage*` in `GenericBodyCopy`. The instance comes from the component that actually owns the receipt. The coordinator binds the session registry and the stage-open result before dispatch. The worker recovers its single request from the heterogeneous kernel payload. Both reversed writes now fail on the incompatible nominal types. The same swap fails in the actual named storage-test constructor.

The registry and stage data declarations have declaration-only modules. The original defining modules expose their original qualified names through type aliases. Importing both implementation modules solely for their types emitted 88 global definitions and failed a relocatable link against the entities object on duplicate symbols. A qualified client of the original modules compiled on both revisions. Its function disassembly matched. The x86-64 request remained 64 bytes with eight-byte alignment, at offset 56 of the 128-byte work component. The layout probe object, exported/undefined symbol sets, and clone kernel disassembly matched.

The coordinator registers whole-domain Layout and TypeIndex reads and a one-query GenericBody write. During a wave the input view pins the template, registry and instance. Each worker owns its private stage, result and clone stack. Dispatch drains launched slots on every return. The coordinator holds borrowed references while pinned, closes the view, publishes accepted stages in order, charges the registry and finishes each ticket. Hold failure discards all peer stages before closing the view. Other failures discard pending stages and return borrowed lanes before graph cancellation. A refused partial clone left its instance empty. A fresh graph retried that same instance after restoring the fixture's allowance and charged exactly 32 published nodes. Both widths drained all owners.

Host 5 used the public Linux x64 pin, LLVM 19.1.7, a Ryzen 9 5900XT and affinity 0,2,4,6. Effective cpuset was 0–31 with 3,071,999 µs quota per 100,000 µs. Each of five paired processes ran four waves of four requests on one live pool, verified every output, then disposed the pool, world and ledger. Median 8,192-node wave times in baseline/candidate order were 4.123/4.100 ms at one worker and 2.577/2.456 ms at four. All twenty large four-worker waves overlapped on each build. Maximum RSS across measured processes was 73,316/73,304 KiB. These timings describe this native fixture. Shared-host noise limits small differences. The registered quota, storage and query checks, qualified companion, and 1/4-worker ASan/LSan and TSan live-pool controls exercised this path. Some TSan launches hit the host personality restriction before entry. Source-level UBSan is unavailable in this configuration.

The semantic session still holds other raw pointers. Its shared stage-open extern and session registry each require one concrete projection here. Changing the stage return in this module alone produced incompatible declarations of the same link symbol. The worker payload, generic graph subject, and dynamically selected ECS component data retain their existing transport contracts. Assignment `5146cf5c-6968-4e41-ad6a-f5cbe0b9044d` carries the controls, coordinate-checked census, source and per-run logs.

## Jenkins 51 — UTF-8 diagnostic read after Wasm memory growth

At `323165245b6254e671aacba105e8dfc903a5affa`, Jenkins reported 512 passes,
one failure and two skips in 515 Node tests. The native UTF-8 test and the
two companion Wasm tests passed. The failing test had already checked that
`tw_create` returned zero for a rejected source when `memory.indexOf` threw
at `playground/tests/compiler-utf8.test.mjs:58`. Console SHA-256
`1a10045d21ca761101ebe53e4ed2f21bd2f7ca22c7e791937b84ab8da29ae9c7`.

Host 5 reproduced the same exception using the checked-in Linux x64 bootstrap,
WASI SDK 34.0 and `bash playground/scripts/build-wasm.sh -DTOWER_IDE_TESTS=OFF`.
A separate trace of the first input, a single NUL, recorded 13,762,560 bytes
before `tw_create` and 13,828,096 afterward. The old view then reported zero
bytes. Reading `tw_last_error` returned offset 6,153,648 with the new size
unchanged. The rejection path assigns the diagnostic into the IDE state's byte
buffer. Its allocation can grow linear memory even though the guest offsets
remain valid.

The Node fixture now acquires a view for each input write and another after
obtaining the diagnostic pointer. It checks the terminating NUL before decoding.
The standalone truncation test likewise allocates its result before taking the
view used to locate the last byte of memory.

From the repository root, `node --test --test-concurrency=1
playground/tests/compiler-utf8.test.mjs` ran with the same portable reactor
(SHA-256 `d20df1dc5dd371122fae9e473bb011b089bccbd93ba5ab99555ad68716bb8c64`)
and the same `TOWER_TEST_LLVM_WASM` for both runs. That companion reactor came
from Pages commit `3d57e291e231171776ea5b77e207749615c64edf`, compiler source
`0823b028fba66eb19de815f4d49d4fdbc0bdc56a`. Its gzip matched the manifest and
its decompressed SHA-256 was `f84fc37c57b2681583a5b4fb4eddd688cae5212916c0ac190e75c2a29510f1f5`.

| Fixture | Pass/fail | Exit | Wall s | User + system s | Peak RSS KiB |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original | 2/1 | 1 | 3.18 | 6.54 + 0.33 | 333468 |
| Repaired | 3/0 | 0 | 3.00 | 6.19 + 0.32 | 347856 |

Ryzen 9 5900XT, 16 cores/32 threads, CPUs 0–31, 30.72 CPU quota, Node v24.22.3,

### Source ownership while checking cyclic imports

The full-owner default-initialization test in receipt 975b3707 stopped inside
`syntax_reader_span` with both address and thread instrumentation on the original
3ae475c2 compiler. The same six test bodies passed with a fixture-only owner.
The ordinary module graph owns the parsed roots and the source for each loaded
module. Its cycle validator set the parser component kind on a default reader
but left the source empty. The span accessor needs the owning source length
even when the caller uses only the match label.

Cycle validation now lends each loaded module's source to its reader for the
duration of the root walk. A failed span lookup records the reader diagnostic
on that module before classifying the declaration. The existing graph walk and
permitted declaration kinds are unchanged. Qualification uses the real
semantic expression owner, its direct companion, and the existing accepted
and rejected cyclic-import fixtures. The earlier fixture-only passes do not
cover the corrected owner walk.

offset 8 in the FoundationNode, the scalar tag of its embedded FoundationType.

`sem_value_binding` while scanning a type-position syntax node and tested its
scalar against SType. The diagnostic identifies the storage and both accesses.
It does not contain the binding's spelling.

The dispatch coordinator freezes the graph for the batch and waits for the
kernels before finishing tickets. Discovery and readiness needed the registered
child constructor or array query for a specific syntax node. Looking up a
same-named value to infer the kind touched data being written under a different
reservation. Commit 056ab5ae reads the registered query ID and kind directly.
The scans keep their existing dependency and suspension rules. At the remaining
sites that classify type syntax, a registered value's type becomes readable
after its producer succeeds. The worker window, leases and dispatch are unchanged.

to the separate types B and A. The retained ordinary compiler prints 8 and 1
for that input. The final implementation preserves both lines. It also preserves
the predecessor's diagnostic on an ordinary global declared with
`type_type()` used as a type before that binding was available.

### Preserve waiting bodies when recovering skipped ordinary roots

In the Ubuntu 24.04 strict comparison of 3cc57ae4, resetting the body cursor
when ordinary roots became eligible admitted work_budget_init ahead of
compiler_world_worker_reserve. This changed the order of generic Entity and
EntityStage specializations and changed the entities object. Simply recovering
a pending prefix on every stalled suffix restored the entities object and both
real decltype tests, but changed the optimized parser-nodes IR on Linux.
Tracing that compile found two recoveries while earlier work was waiting, at
node_payload_size and lr_reserve_result(LRActionGrowth). Stock and trial
admitted the same bodies in a different sequence. The first emitted difference
was the control temporary in lr_propagation_solve_components_result.

Keep the ordinary cursor through root admission, return progress for completed
work, and preserve Waiting while an earlier body has outstanding work. Only
when a pump would otherwise finish after walking an exhausted suffix does it
look for a still-pending earlier function. It uses the existing signature/body
demand check and owns no new persistent state. The coordinator performs this
check after worker publication and error handling.

Using the same Ubuntu LLVM 19.1.1 host, an unchanged bootstrap comparer
accepted all four entities targets. At one and four workers, the Linux parser
object and optimized IR matched the public pin byte for byte. Both actual
decltype owners and their directly selected companions rejected a changed
expected byte at compiletime_case.tower:18:5 and passed after restoration at
both widths. A runtime call still diagnosed missing_body_value. The host 6
receipt c5a50ceb contains the three cursor comparisons, the rejected
intermediate, resource measurements and the independent release gates.

The Pages manifest at `9788bd66ff4d90b174bbe73c33aa6f68c4e9b5af` hashes to

To reproduce the seven registrations with an existing image, run from the
checkout root with Node 24.

```sh
pages=9788bd66ff4d90b174bbe73c33aa6f68c4e9b5af
images=$(mktemp -d)
git show "$pages:deployment-manifest.json" > "$images/manifest.json"
for asset in tower.wasm tower-threads.wasm; do
    git show "$pages:$asset" > "$images/$asset" || exit 1
    (cd "$images" && jq -r --arg a "$asset" '.assets[$a] + "  " + $a' manifest.json | sha256sum -c -) || exit 1
    TOWER_TEST_WASM="$images/$asset" node --test --test-concurrency=1 \
        --test-name-pattern='^fast and graph: ' playground/tests/fast-interpreter.test.mjs || exit 1
done
```

## Native syntax emission fixtures at 401c402e

Host 3 audited the parser-only Release entry on the published

Its focused entry, also called by the native frontend emission selector,

handles, runs the entire suite twice and compares live buffer and entity

The late nullable/recursive FIRST and edited Z comparison uses

grammar and refusal walk, 2 for Bedrock, 3 for Bedrock with reserved helper
names, 4 for mutually nullable rules and ordinary/reachable/Statement

imbalance, 503 for a result/error or tree/ID mismatch and 501 for an
unsuccessful otherwise conforming baseline. Zero indicates completion.
The independent oracle uses linear name and FIRST sets over the same shared
entities. The comparison checks the ordered production trees, name metadata,
production indices and helper provenance. Both emissions, their roots and
each fixture's private vectors and entity owner are released.

GDB sampled the original and moved executables and the actual captured selected guests at compiler jobs 1 and 4. Across 16 handoffs, a separate pthread entered the exact exported address passed to `pthread_create`, with the caller's stack payload. The caller acquired the finished semaphore and compared 42. It stored 84 and posted the release semaphore. The worker compared 84 in the same slot. All 16 joins returned zero before the 32 semaphore destructions. In the jobs-4 direct replay, both comparisons addressed `0x7ffd2aad8ae0` and the thread entry was `0x5d721564dd90`. These addresses belong to that process. Original and moved standalone allocation traces each recorded two 32-byte signal allocations and one 8-byte pthread slot, then frees of all three pointers.

Injected failure of either semaphore initialization returned 3 and destroyed the one initialized semaphore. Refused pthread creation returned 4 and destroyed both signals. Each result held for original and moved standalones, in try and wait. Dropping the explicit export flag still left the worker dynamically visible with this published linker. Localizing the worker definition in a disposable object removed it from the dynamic symbols. Lookup then failed, returning 4 in both standalone modes and failing the polling assertion in each selected guest.

- A successful next construct has a node and an empty diagnostic. On a

- A span requires an existing node with a match component. Its start must
  be within the source and its length must fit the remaining bytes. A

  offset. Style text likewise requires the expected length and bytes.
  Parser traversal, fixture building, allocation tracking and formatting
  continue through their original helpers.

**Coverage and reproduction.** Native ELF recording suites passed
normally, under ASan with leak checks and a trapping UBSan SDK layout
boundary, and under TSan with four pthreads × four independent repetitions
per suite. The packet has maps, instrumented objects, startup errors

reported shapes. Draw owns execution in its production renderer. Physical
Windows, other adapters and a 16384-command GPU workload remain open.

### External Tower source to a Linux Vulkan executable on slot 12

The published rendering SDK parent was `851e26d8aa6f3b6e492668f4b9c5655184ca2c85`.
The packaged compiler (`7430bdb39f73b285687fedb2945d370eaf51d2cc2fa289e5e0041cc15ad1b896`)

It reuses the published clear recorder and CPU row oracle. The shaderless clear
needs no shader assets or device-function-pointer import. The original row and
oracle blobs from `3dd5f11f`, a direct child of `a580e70a`, matched this SDK byte for byte.

**Driver and binding.** The existing image smoke's exported main collided with
the bundled runtime's main in source-to-executable mode, including with
`--library`. The original source compiled with `--library --emit object`.
`towerc --link-executable` then linked it with the SDK and loader alone and it
matched the retained cc-linked smoke's successful output. Adding the full runtime
object to that link reproduced the duplicate symbol. Renaming the copied smoke
entry and calling it from the top level also worked. The ordinary clear entry
uses top-level statements. One `towerc --emit exe` invocation compiled its
source and linked the SDK, loader and libatomic on `x86_64-linux-gnu`.
The exec trace contains Clang compiling the shipped runtime IR. Tower linked
the PIE. Its SHA-256 was `6a33bb255a2690dc18fa106c2cfe3ad397e6f1977d331162d6545694457f05a0`.
The loader bound all seven application SDK imports to the rebuilt sixteen-entry
`libtower_graphics.so` (`2d924e642e1820a8651015802bf56c332215178db373709ee80a5f5d91be76bf`).
An absent explicit SDK path returned 1 at build time. Removing the runtime
search path gave loader exit 127.

**Device evidence.** Slot 12 selected the RTX 3090, UUID
`cd3d9791fe794e0b3ec29fc16b74d31c`, Vulkan 1.3.289, NVIDIA 565.57.01,
physical device/family/queue 0/0/0. A second run of the same ELF selected
llvmpipe, Vulkan 1.3.230, Mesa 22.3.6, LLVM 15.0.6. Each Khronos plus sync
validation count was zero after teardown. Both traces showed SDK submit
returning zero, a successful wait on that fence, map and unmap, followed by
SDK retirement of the same view, image and memory in order before device
destruction. The debugger dumped the mapped 16 bytes at unmap and the 32 caller

dumps on both devices. The guarded hash was
`19e6f721a40fd19ec72a3985f0a91989fb4c3faa85f7b207088a80922303d374`.
The ordinary source and split Tower links produced different ELFs and identical
checked output on each device. The CPU pitch-7, span-19 and short-source cases

**Incremental build.** The SDK's library script and direct compiler invocations
run unconditionally. The native project's CMake custom commands pass compiler

### Linux counted completion through the selected queue submitter

Slot 12 compared SDK `ea88e0009af4eec24cd64db9d784f843e1413ccc`
with the helper and typed recording matrix in
`2bf097e076107ad57d04cb307462fa45258132a6`. The SDK's capture returned
on every submit error and used a device-wide idle after a failed fence
wait. The historical helper constructed its own submit and called the
loader directly. Applying it verbatim would discard the descriptor prepared
by the selected end callback and bypass the external application's DSO.

The counted capture now passes the signed result of its existing submit to
`vk_complete_submission`. The caller retains the device, queue, prepared
batch, primary, fresh fence and referenced allocations. The helper borrows
the handles for completion. Only a successful fence wait permits the map.
The first failing Vulkan call is printed with its signed result. Both submit
OOMs return immediately. Other submit failures skip the fence and drain
the same queue. A fence wait reporting loss permits release. Other wait
failures drain the same queue. Success or loss from that drain permits
release with a failed capture. Any further error flushes both diagnostics
and aborts while the owner's defers are still pending.

**Clear ownership audit.** The raw counted and external counted entries
share `counted_capture`. They import allocation helpers and Vulkan
declarations from `readback_clear`, but neither executes its clear/readback
submission. The raw clear fixture and the external `clear_and_read` have
separate synchronous owners and independent submit/wait blocks. The Win64
packaging recipe copies the raw clear source and uses a pinned counted
capture. This change is confined to the Linux counted dependency path.
Clear error retirement is a separate integration obligation. The published
Win64 inputs and callback/DSO ABI are preserved.

### Scoped Vulkan staging readback on slot 12

On published rendering SDK `b1db999ae7b5d77e9ec261a1f5d0b6f822db6b4b`,
raw clear and SDK clear borrow a 32-byte pitched destination. Counted capture
reads two count/command prefixes and checks two guarded images. All three
perform the same whole-allocation map, conditional invalidation and unmap
after their submit/fence helper succeeds. The application owns the staging
allocation throughout. The proposed extraction lends mapped bytes to a
synchronous typed consumer so each caller keeps its own layout and output.

The frozen parent passed both clear and both counted entry points on the
slot 12 RTX 3090. NVIDIA 565.57.01 exposes host-visible memory types 3, 4
and 5 with flags 0x6, 0xe and 0x7. Each is coherent. This device can
exercise the normal coherent copy. A recorded Vulkan boundary is required
to exercise the other visibility branch.

**Implementation and checks.** `vk_read_mapped` takes the device, memory,
selected memory flags, diagnostic labels and a typed synchronous consumer.
The helper owns the mapping from a successful map through lexical unmap.
The clear consumer borrows the pitched destination. The counted consumer
borrows the mapped bytes and consumes both records at the supplied stride.
Neither stores the mapped address. All three sites call the helper only
after `vk_complete_submission` returns true. Submit, queue-drain and
destruction code stayed at their existing ownership boundaries.

On the RTX 3090 (API 1.3.289, device 0, graphics family 0, queue 0), raw
clear and the external SDK clear reproduced the 32-byte reference
`19e6f721a40fd19ec72a3985f0a91989fb4c3faa85f7b207088a80922303d374`.
Raw and SDK counted-core13 reproduced the 112-byte reference
`a49420a8cae9cf5185a8d8dc1d18556dce6b332ec223f9e22aa00eabef7436e6`.
Both revisions printed identical ordinary output and zero validation
warnings/errors. The original rendering CPU rows and oracle match
`3dd5f11f`, a direct child of the requested `a580e70a`. That parent
itself has neither fixture file. The checks use the existing two-row
oracle and the counted sample including each prefix, row gap and guard.

The [recording executable](../scaffolding/library/graphics/vulkan/readback_mapping_checks.tower)
checks map/copy/unmap for coherent memory and map/invalidate/copy/unmap
for noncoherent memory. A refused map stops at map. A refused invalidate
unmaps once and skips the consumer. A consumer that rejects the row pitch
also unmaps once. All failure cases preserved every guard. Both operations
received the same device and allocation, offset zero and VK_WHOLE_SIZE.

Slot 12 captured seven debugger traces per entry on each revision. The
boundary identified the transfer-destination-only buffer at creation and
matched its binding against the later map, invalidate and unmap. It checked
the submitted fence and a successful real wait before every map. Removing
the coherent flag from the application's local copy of the memory-type
list exercised successful invalidation on the otherwise-coherent device.
Injected map −5 and invalidate −2 preserved each caller's signed diagnostic.
All 32 clear bytes stayed guarded, and counted capture published zero of its
four comparison outputs. An out-of-memory submit skipped the fence. An
injected wait −1 drained the submitting queue. A second drain error −2
aborted. None of the three submission failures reached map. In twelve
two-queue trials, the second queue remained pending throughout recovery and
completed after its own host signal. Hardware noncoherent visibility and
real driver-reported faults remain open.

The Linux raw fixtures and the two external SDK applications resolved
the shared module from their selected Foundation root. ELF imports and both
Win64 counted import tables matched the parent. The ordinary and CRT PEs
still import shader creation and counted draw from the graphics DLL. The
16-entry Linux DSO, DLL and import library reproduced hashes beginning
`2d924e64`, `8fc64f24` and `2d56f882`. Win64 evidence covers both links.
Slot 11 owns execution and its separate command-import qualification.

**Costs.** Slot 12 used the packaged compiler `7430bdb3`, LLVM 19.1.7,
Linux x86-64, EPYC 7282 (16 cores, 32 logical, 15.36 CPU quota) and one
application process and submission thread at a time. After one warmup,
seven paired samples alternated revision order. The uninstrumented processes
include validation, device setup and retirement. A separate Tower probe
bracketed the post-fence operation through unmap in each source revision.
Those intervals include the caller's copying, comparisons and diagnostic
formatting. Every sample reproduced the complete ordinary stdout.

| Entry | Median wall s, parent → candidate | Median CPU s | Largest peak RSS KiB | Median post-fence µs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Raw clear | 0.30 → 0.31 | 0.30 → 0.30 | 91864 → 91812 | 4.57 → 4.40 |
| SDK clear | 0.30 → 0.30 | 0.29 → 0.29 | 91744 → 91800 | 3.91 → 3.95 |
| Raw counted | 0.31 → 0.31 | 0.30 → 0.30 | 94908 → 94876 | 12.79 → 12.77 |
| SDK counted | 0.31 → 0.31 | 0.31 → 0.31 | 94848 → 94856 | 11.46 → 11.66 |

All intervals had overlapping observed ranges. The Tower allocator recorded
two grants totaling 152 bytes per clear and five totaling 3376 bytes per
counted process, with peaks of 152 and 1752 live bytes respectively. Every
grant was released on both revisions. The compiler emitted direct consumer
code for the measured entries. There is no extra staging copy or allocation.

Three warm compilation samples at each worker count checked every generated
object or executable against its revision's one-worker artifact. The raw
object took median 0.64 → 0.65 s wall at one worker and 0.75 → 0.75 s at four.
The external counted executable took 1.26 → 1.33 s at one and 1.38 → 1.45 s
at four. Median CPU seconds were 0.63 → 0.64, 0.85 → 0.85, 1.26 → 1.33
and 1.56 → 1.63 respectively. Largest peak RSS in the same order was
109960 → 110452, 115300 → 115888, 130164 → 131464 and 135688 → 136348 KiB.
Three additional one-worker counted builds with `--timings` located most of
the increase in the compiler's `after` bucket (median 158.6 → 218.5 ms).
The final link stayed near 2 ms. The phase totals do not isolate generic
specialization from other frontend work.

**Instrumentation and reproduction.** LLVM ASan-instrumented executables
passed all four healthy device paths. The recording matrix passed with
leak detection enabled, including both error returns. Full-process LSan on
raw clear reported 3511 bytes in eight allocations on each revision with
validation-layer frames. The TSan-instrumented SDK clear stopped before
main at the container personality restriction (139). There is no native
Tower UBSan profile. None of these runs establishes hardware behavior for
noncoherent staging.

and [Win64 build](../scaffolding/library/graphics/vulkan/osd_checks/tower_client/counted_win64/build.sh).
Assignment `6a147ede-e672-4290-980c-f788e80113f7` includes the bounded Git
bundle, binaries, dependency roots, exact commands, raw samples, link maps,
device/fault traces and checksums. An early extraction left VK_WHOLE_SIZE
outside the counted recorder's import scope. The shared ABI now defines
the range constants and both roots compile. Initial instrumentation needed
an explicit Linux i64 ssize_t, an observer for the inlined recording helper
and foreground debugger stops before checking the exit status. The final
packet retains the failed attempts and the successful replays.
